# Facts on record

## Execution model

- Two execution paths share parser and phases and differ at the end: the walk interpreter (`fortress file.fss`) and the bytecode compiler (`fortress compile` + `run`) (`repo-internals.md:95-129`).
- The static type checker (Scala, `scala_src/typechecker/`) runs only on the compile path; `walk` turns it off and there is no switch to make it run in the interpreter (`repo-internals.md:127`); every "type error" seen from the interpreter is a run-time dispatch failure.
- `fortress typecheck` checks against `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, not the interpreter's prelude, so it is not an oracle for interpreter programs (ledger row 69); making the checker usable on interpreter programs means giving it the interpreter's prelude, which is not a ledger row and not on the worklist as a separate item (it falls under worklist item 2, compiler-path library parity).
- The code generator lowers every type to a JVM reference type: `RR64` to the runtime class `FRR64`, no `dadd`/`dmul` anywhere in the generated loop (shown in bytecode, `perf-probes/boxing/javap/`); arrays are library objects over `get`/`put`, not `double[]` (`repo-internals.md:129`).
- On microGPT-shaped array code boxing is the dominant representational cost, 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]` in Java models of the program's three kernels, and nothing microGPT-shaped compiles: the compiler prelude lacks the array types, with `Array`, `Vector` and `Array3` undefined in `FlatArrays.fsi` (row 305, wider than row 72). On the interpreter, the only path that runs the kernels, 43.5% is the AST walk, 32.3% environment lookup, 5.2% type dispatch and 0% number representation (JFR on `krows`). The two one-line runtime defects the probe found are fixed (rows 302, 303; the next two entries), and no array type goes into the compiler prelude: the arrays reach the compiled path with the one library (POSITIONS, the library route). A failed compile leaves a 0-byte jar in the bytecode cache (`perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md`).
- The boxing probe's scalar-loop reading, 156× primitive Java with boxing about 2% of it, is of the tree before rung 0's two fixes (rows 302, 303; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`); of the costs it named, `countedseqloop`'s boxed indices and closure call (about 7%) and the representational rest (about 30%) are unaddressed (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`).
- The eager debug string of `BaseTask.inATransaction()` is fixed: the message is built only under the `debug` flag (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:248`; row 302; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`).
- `FFloatLiteral`'s String round trip is fixed: the literal caches its `double` instead of re-parsing its text in `asRR64()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FFloatLiteral.java`; row 303; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`).
- The benchmark numbers on record from 2026-09-15 (`bench1t` 9.3441 s, `bench1h` 6.0732 s) were taken on a quieter machine: the same unmodified tree measured 13.0566 s and 8.8159 s in another session, so absolute seconds are not comparable across sessions and only a before/after pair taken in one session is (`compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`).
- `ant compileAll` leaves the bytecode cache holding no library jars: the first `fortress compile` after a rebuild of the compiler clears `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/`, and `fortress run` then dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: fortress/CompilerLibrary$GeneratorZZ32`; the library-order recompile of `repo-internals.md:170-179` restores it, about two minutes.
- The compiled path's bytecode cache can come up empty after a library-order rebuild that reports exit 0; re-running the same commands one at a time produced the jars (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`).
- Generic instantiations are stamped out at class-load time by ASM rewriting of template bytecode (`InstantiatingClassloader.java`, `repo-internals.md:129`); a size is in the stamped class's name (`pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, `perf-probes/nat/java.md` § 1; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md`), and its descriptor in a stamped class is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` ("A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics).
- Implicit parallelism: `for` is parallel unless every generator is `seq`; the elements of a tuple and the operands of an operator are evaluated in parallel implicit threads (`tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:59`; row 265). `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the work-stealing pool; there is no explicit threading in any of our programs.
- The compile path's checker cannot check `nat` parameters at all (see "The checker and the one library" below): this no longer holds. The checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters ("The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters" below), and a sized program loads and runs compiled ("A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics). Sizes in types (`nat` parameters) are "instantiated at runtime" by the specification (`trait-parameters.tex`, natparams); they check shapes when a value is made or passed; no optimization is built on them anywhere. A `nat`-typed parameter does not unify statically with a run-time-built array (row 23); the interpreter matches at dispatch, and a mismatch reads "Failed to find any matching overload", uncatchable (row 83). A literal size does unify (row 23's positive half).
- **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not codegen.** The Working Draft's `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49`, kept in `Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:61-65` marked "Not allowed") stops on both paths with a syntax error at `excludes`, because the grammar gives an object no `excludes` clause (`Specification/basic/objects.tex:84-86`; `reviews/spec-refused-examples/probes/SpecNothing.fss` and its captures). Without that clause, `fortress compile` and `fortress walk` give the identical single error, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss`, `.txt`; `reviews/spec-refused-examples/probes/SpecNothingNoExcludes.fss`). A where clause on an object declaration does not bind a type variable used in that declaration's extends clause in either implementation. `CodeGen.forObjectDeclPrePass` would refuse the declaration a second time at codegen — `header.getWhereClause().isNone()` is one of its `canCompile` conditions (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4093`) — but nothing reaches it. This is the mechanism behind the library's comment on its parametric `Nothing[\T\]`, "Obviously ought to be a non-parametric singleton when we get where clauses working" (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1449-1450`), and it is why both worlds must spell the empty case some other way.
- **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's** (`compile-ladder/rung-export-var/`). Both paths assume an api and its implementing component share a name: `fortress link` and `walk` print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path", and the compiled run dies with `NoClassDefFoundError`. The assumption is `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`'s fallback to the api's own name (`linker/Linker.java:72-76`); only `LinkShell`'s `alink`/`clink` register another. The specification resolves an imported api to a component that exports it (`Specification/basic/components/overview.tex:33-35`), and the team reserved the codegen half in `CodeGen.java:411-441`, `:1856`, `:6599-6606`. Gated as an expected failure by `compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`.
- **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it** (`compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/probes/SpanAbsorb.fss` and `SpanAbsorb.txt`; ledger row 359). `createSpan` (`parser/Fortress.rats:145-157`) trims back over space characters only; a declaration ending in `end` is unaffected. So a comment-only library edit is not neutral at the syntax-tree level, and a before-and-after comparison of parse trees or diagnostics maps positions back first (`compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/parse-compare.sh`, `remap-lines.py`).
- **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees** (`compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md`, section 4.1): `throw new FortressError((FObject) Driver.getFortressLibrary().getRootValue(name))` from a `builtinPrimitive` method reaches `Evaluator.forTry` unchanged; the helper is `Int.overflow()` (`interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:258-261`). Gated by the `overflows(...)` assertions of `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`. The natives that raise `IntegerOverflow` so are those of "The interpreter's integer rules" and "Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit" under Landed semantics, with the narrowing checks `Int.rc` and `NN32.rc` (row 347 closed). Every other Java exception is mapped as before (`FunctionClosure.java:188-196`), so row 336's division by zero still ends the run.
- **The compiled run's class loader takes its first load of a name under the JDK's class-loading lock, and a generic arm's first load is safe on four threads** (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1, 11, 12; row 417). `InstantiatingClassloader.loadClass` runs under `getClassLoadingLock(name)`, as the JDK's `ClassLoader.loadClass` does; no loader in the tree registers as parallel-capable, so the lock is the loader's own monitor, and the explicit loads (`RTHelpers.loadClosureClass`, `RTHelpers.getRTTIclass`, the union instantiation) are under it too. Gated by `compiler_tests/FirstLoadThreadsRungG` in the gate's four-thread stage.
- **Walk chooses between a generic declaration and another on their declared domains, so the order they are written in no longer decides** (`compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 5.1; POSITIONS, "The static-parameter sentence goes"; row 548). `OverloadedFunction.bestMatchInternal` keeps a candidate by `moreSpecificDeclaration` (`interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:1420-1427`): beside a generic function or constructor the declared domains are compared through the symbolic instantiation (`instanceHolding`, `:1376-1391`), otherwise the instances' domains; a generic trait's functional method and a generic dotted method keep the instance comparison. A chosen generic instance that converts an argument dispatches again (`convertedCall`, `:1307-1324`), not for overloaded methods. The symbolic instantiation is keyed by each static parameter's kind and bounds (`GenericFunctionOrMethod.java:57-68`; row 478, fixed), not by a `where` clause (`FGenericFunction.java:49-51`). Gated by `tests/DispatchDeclaredDomain.fss`, `DispatchConvertedAgain.fss` and `GenericOverloadBoundsApart.fss`.
- **Walk's load check reads a generic declaration beside a plain one on declared domains, and covers an overlap through `comprises` clauses, where its parameter-by-parameter check refuses** (`compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` sections 5.3 and 5.4; POSITIONS, "Conversions never change which declaration runs" and "The `comprises` passages read at the level of values (PLAN item 26, row 491)"; row 492, fixed). Both run only where the parameter-by-parameter check refuses (`OverloadedFunction.java:497-500`). For one own generic beside a plain declaration, `validOnDeclaredDomains` (`:693-722`) compares declared domains under the return-type rule and accepts an overlap that plain declarations below both cover, reading each parameter of the generic as the types whose intersection holds its values: a type parameter as its bounds that name no static parameter, a type that mentions a static parameter as `Any`, a non-type static parameter as no reason to refuse (`genericOverlapCovered`, `:728-778`; `intersectionPieces`, `:917-976`; row 552, fixed); for two plain declarations with an unrelated parameter pair, `overlapCovered` (`:814-825`; `overlapPieces`, `:986-1030`) cuts the overlap by the `comprises` clauses and needs every part inside one declaration below both, refusing what it cannot settle. Two generic declarations take the parameter-by-parameter check alone (Q4 = (1)). Gated by `tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss`, `ComprisesCoverReturn.fss`, `GenericBesidePlainTwoBounds.fss` and `GenericBesidePlainOverlapShapes.fss` (row 552), and the refusals `XXXGenericBesidePlainReturnRule.fss`, `XXXComprisesMeetUncovered`, `XXXComprisesCoverReturnWrong` and `XXXOverloadExistentialMeetWalk.fss` (row 539). Walk checks the closure of the main component's `comprises` clauses (row 551), not yet the library's (rows 595, 596), another component's (row 551) or an object expression's (row 597; "Walk checks at load the `comprises` clauses of the program's main component ..." below).
- **Walk instantiates a generic declaration declared to return `Any`** (`compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 3; row 157, fixed): `MakeInferenceSpecific.forAnyType` is a no-op like `forTraitType` (`interpreter/evaluator/MakeInferenceSpecific.java:72-75`). Gated by `tests/GenericReturningAny.fss`; row 496's probe `PlainBesideZZ32` prints `Marker[ZZ32]` under walk. The visitor has no case for 11 of the AST's 18 concrete type classes, of which only the dimension forms can be written as a return type.
- **Walk checks at load the `comprises` clauses of the program's main component, and its harness names an expected refusal at load** (`compile-ladder/rung-walk-load-check/REPORT.md`; row 552 fixed, row 551 for the main component's clauses). `BuildEnvironments.checkComprisesClauses`, called from `Driver.evalComponent` once every component's types are built, reads the declarations as written and asks every extender of a closed trait of the main component for the traits chapter's three eligible forms, reading a generic child's extenders across the whole program; the library's clauses (rows 595, 596), another component's (row 551), an object expression (row 597) and the clause's other half, that a listed type extends each instantiation (row 598), are not read. A file `Name.fss` of `tests/` names its refusal in `Name.test` by `load_exception_contains` (`FileTests.java`, `InterpreterTest.loadRefusalKeys`): a plain test passes when walk refuses the program at load as named, an `XXX` test when the program loads and runs clean; a failure while the top-level variables are initialized counts as a refusal at load. Gated by `tests/ComprisesUnlistedExtender`, `ComprisesGenericChildUnlistedExtender`, `GenericBesidePlainOverlapShapes` and the `XXX` files of rows 22, 487, 534, 544, 549, 597 and 598.
## The checker and the one library

- The one library binds its natives with `builtinPrimitive("…")`: 424 live bindings in nine files (445 written, 20 inside comments, one `RR32` binding fewer since `RR32` became a sibling of `RR64`), 125 of them in `FortressLibrary.fss`, and the rest of the library is plain Fortress. Beside them, walk loads the Java classes of 32 objects of `native component`s by name and binds `true`, `false` and `Any` at start-up. The interpreter's glue classes take the evaluator's boxed values and cannot be reused by the compiled path; the compiler's natives are static Java methods over plain Java values, called through `import java`: 369 public static helpers in 25 classes of `nativeHelpers/`, which the compiler prelude's 366 native bodies call. Matched by owner, name and signature, then by operation: 147 of the bindings are bound on the compiled path already, so only their binding text changes; 61 have a helper that nothing binds yet, 25 of them under a name the compiler prelude binds to another helper, the 12 wrapping operators among them (row 348); 139 need a new static helper, written from 132 glue classes of about 0.7K lines; and 78 need something else, 36 methods of native I/O objects (`Writer`, `BufferedWriter`, `FileReadStream`, `FileWriteStream`, `Reader`) and 42 with no compiled analogue (reflection, `Thread`, the native arrays, the task trace). The prelude and what it imports hold 369 of the bindings. Every program's output needs the I/O objects: `println` writes through `stdOut`, a native `Writer` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4340-4343`, `Library/Writer.fss:20-24`), so the first compiled program on the one library needs `Writer`'s natives. MicroGPT calls `nanoTime`, which needs a new helper (the compiled one returns `RR64`), imports `System`, whose top-level `args` calls `getProgramArgsPrim`, which has no compiled analogue, when the component loads (`Library/System.fss:28`), and its arrays reach `NativeArray`, which has none either. Source: `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape.md` § 2, its scripts and every binding's class under `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape/count/` (`classified.tsv`). The nine rungs that move walk onto the helpers are PLAN's phase 4, the natives; which construct is the one binding text is PLAN item 35 (the `import java` entry under The territory map).
- `fortress compile Library/FortressLibrary.fss` as it is: 1,417 errors, all in DISAMBIGUATE, all name collisions because both preludes are in scope; an artifact. With `FortressLibrary` made the prelude (a driver over `Shell`'s public entry points, no tracked file changed), disambiguation passes with zero errors (`perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`). What the checker then reports on the library, which the gate's checker-count and distance stages measure at every landing, is in "The true distance to the switch-over" below; it checks `nat` and `int` static parameters and refuses a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` one by name, with no crash ("The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters" below).
- **The Scala type checker does not implement `nat` static parameters at all** does not hold: the checker implements `nat` and `int` static parameters, a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` one has a named error, not rules ("The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters" below), and a sized program runs compiled ("A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics). The title was the first measurement of the checker against the library (`perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`).
- **Between the interpreter's library and bytecode stands the checker, not desugaring or code generation** (`perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen.md`, the library pushed through DESUGAR and CODEGEN with the checker's failures caught per top-level declaration, validated on `CompilerLibrary.fss` where the method reproduces the ordinary compile exactly). On the nested tower, of `FortressLibrary.fss`'s 446 top-level declarations the checker passed 237 clean, reported errors on 97 and crashed on 112 (81 `makeInferenceArg` nyi, 29 `TraitType→IntExpr`, the `nat` gap, both since closed); DESUGAR and OVERLOADREWRITE then report zero diagnostics on all of it; CODEGEN emitted 275 and refused 313, of which only **5 were on declarations the checker checked clean** (four a numeric static argument, one a method call on an intersection-typed receiver); the rest were missing annotations on unchecked declarations (227), `Juxt` (53), the checker's shadow rather than a missing visitor (a juxtaposition is what the checker resolves into an application or a method call, and all 53 were on declarations it crashed on or refused, `desugar-codegen.md` § 2.2, § 6), the missing visitor `Label` (1), `nat` static arguments (14), malformed overload sets (7); `canCompile` refused nothing and no native binding was missing. Two obstacles the error counts do not show: the compile path's own `extends Object` pre-desugaring (`Shell.java:371-386`) adds 712 of the 960 checker errors in the prelude apis and 618 of 1,204 in the component under its own setting, rejecting every generic instantiated at a tuple type (row 412; the gate's stages run under the bound `Any` instead); and overload dispatch generation did not terminate on the nested library's exclusion graph (1,046 s, stopped by hand). On the flat library the dispatch generator finishes and the checker's figures are the gate's ("The true distance to the switch-over" below).
- **The `nat` plan's minimal design works as a shadow, and the road is three batches, not one** (`perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md`, `shadow.patch`, 22 captures): the design is built, the checker half as "The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters" below and the run-time half as "A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics. What the shadow established that still describes the tree: a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` static parameter gives a checker error naming the kind; the size crash had a Java site as well as a Scala one (`compiler/codegen/FnNameInfo.java`, any method on a nat-parameterized receiver), and a compiled sized program needs a run-time kind for sizes, since `isOprKind` (`Naming.java:103`) is the run time's only other static-argument kind predicate; the api has 25 declarations with a dead size (E3, POSITIONS, "Sizes"), and the per-declaration check of `trait Number` alone takes minutes without the trait table's memo ("`TypeAnalyzer.parents` and `excludesClause` are memoized per trait table" below).
- **The shadow's two `subarray` errors were the rule's, fixed in two lines, and the checker's slowdown is the tree's own** (`perf-probes/nat/followup.md`, captures `followup/`). A size left unsolved after comparing two declarations' return types was counted as a failure (`Formula.imp`, `Formula.scala:168`, via `OverloadingOracle.satisfiesReturnTypeRule` and `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:145`); the two-line relaxation there proved unneeded, `keep-size-params` alone clearing the `subarray` refusal ("The return-type rule now reads a size as it reads a type parameter" below); the denied shape was `Vector`'s, `Matrix`'s and C4's slicing, so the rule carries it. The slowdown: 87 % of 39,287 JFR samples in `TypeAnalyzerUtil.substitute` from `TypeAnalyzer.parents` (`:722`) and `excludesClause` (`:747`), the second recursing over every supertrait, no sample in the size track; the memo that removes it lives on `TraitTable` ("`TypeAnalyzer.parents` and `excludesClause` are memoized per trait table" below). Five declarations of the library report one error each under the size rule that they did not without it (`FortressLibrary.fss:129, :2248, :2594, :3064, :3151` at the shadow's lines), three of one shape (a `__bigOperatorSugar` body whose return type is taken from the nullary api overload, `.fsi:96` not `:98`, no size in them) and `__builtinFactory2` a likely true positive (branches `Array2[\T,0,s0,0,s1\]` and `__DefaultArray2[\T,b0,s0,b1,s1\]` join only under its own `if b0=0 AND b1=0` guard); they are read in the distance stage's table, not re-traced.
- **The Java site of the size crash is nine lines, and a sized program runs compiled with a stamped descriptor per literal** (`perf-probes/nat/java.md`, `java/java-shadow.patch`, captures `java/`). `FnNameInfo.boundsFor` (`compiler/codegen/FnNameInfo.java:162-173`) returned a `TypeArg` for every static-parameter kind; with `KindNat`/`KindInt` mapped to `IntArg(IntRef name)`, the identity `STypesUtil.staticParamToArg` already gives (`STypesUtil.scala:338-339`), every `cannot be cast to IntExpr` crash is gone (built as kind-correct static arguments in `FnNameInfo.boundsFor`, "The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters" below). `bool`, `dim`, `unit` and `opr` keep the latent `boundsFor` bug, which still returns a type argument for every kind but `nat` and `int` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/FnNameInfo.java:165-180`). The mangled name for a sized receiver keeps the size as its own symbol (`NamingCzar.forIntRef` `:1894-1897`, `forIntBase` `:1889-1892`). A descriptor is asked for at `MethodInstantiater.rttiReference:117-138` and `CodeGen.generateTypeReference:5784-5793`; a symbol needs no descriptor (the template holds `Box⟦k⟧$RTTIc`), only literals reach the loader, and the landed `RTTIsize` (design B with the factory, POSITIONS, "The run-time size design is B") has no `javaRep`, the shadow's placeholder. The stamping tool `java/StampSizeRTTI.java` of the shadow is replaced by the factory. The gate cannot see a classpath shadow.
- **A size at run time can follow the opr path, 28 lines, and a size in value position is 25 more** (`perf-probes/nat/runtime.md`, `runtime/design-a.patch`, `runtime/value-position.patch`, captures `runtime/r1-r8`): design A, a size static argument exempted from needing an RTTI class the way `isOprKind` exempts oprs, is not taken (POSITIONS, "The run-time size design is B"); design B is built with the factory. What the probe established that still holds: the library's own source uses four size literals (0, 1, 2, 3) in 85 places; a size in value position is one `CONST` op in the substitute-at-load channel that the loader turns into an integer `LDC`, the specification's `makeVector` needing it not, the sentence beside it (`trait-parameters.tex:83-86`) and any array library needing it (built, "A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics); a type test on a size is an `INSTANCEOF` on the value's own class, also with the size a static parameter of the enclosing function; `pTypeCase` failing with the shadow off is row 340's shape, a `typecase` as a whole function body whose clauses need a coercion, and says nothing about generics (`reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md` § 2). Design A's fourth gap (a size read inside a method of a sized object, expanded inside `Buf⟦3⟧$RTTIc` whose map does not bind `s`) is design A's own and does not exist under B.
- **The brief's three size probes, measured under both designs: design A's default falls to the brief's own stop condition, and the checker rung carries a four-line defect** (`perf-probes/nat/size-probes.md`, programs, patches and captures under `perf-probes/nat/size-probes/`). (1) A dispatched overload arm generic in a size (row 214's three arms with a catch-all, the argument typed `Any`): the checker's `normalizeUA` dropped every `nat` parameter from a generic arrow (`scala_src/types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:449, 485`) and the return-type rule then compared two renamed sizes; four code lines fix it, landed as `keep-size-params` (row 410, closed). Past the checker, design A links, runs and silently picks the catch-all for every size-generic arm, because its dispatcher tests `INSTANCEOF Vec⟦FRR64,s⟧`, a class named with the arm's own symbol (`compiler/OverloadSet.java:1015, 1077`); design B's dispatcher, as built, is right on all four programs and the arms read their sizes (`dispatch-b.patch` and its 14-line extends-clause piece, `extends-b.patch`; row 411). 108	## Landed semantics
109	
110	- The compiled world's mutable-variable cell holds `fortress.AnyType.Any`, the language's top type, not `runtimeValues.FValue`: a compiled closure is not an `FValue`, so a mutable variable of arrow type, local or top-level, failed the verifier (`runtimeValues/MutableFValue.java:18-32`, `runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:20,27-28,144,152,226`; `compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/P15LocalArrow.fss`, `P16LocalArrowTask.fss`).
111	- **A numeral's value reaches the compiled world intact as of the repair batch of 2026-09-18.** `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr` chooses a numeral's representation by `BigInteger.bitLength()` `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs, and `FIntLiteral.asNN64` reads the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 keeps, so `4294967295` and `18446744073709551615` keep their values (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86`) and the compiled run agrees with `walk` (row 317; `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`).
112	- **The repair turns one loud failure into a quiet value, and the value it prints is wrong even though the value it holds is right.** `simpleIntLiteralArith.fromBigInteger` sends an `IntLiteral` result of bit length 64 or more to the string branch (`nativeHelpers/simpleIntLiteralArith.java:31-32`), so `n: NN64 = x + x + 1` for `x = 9223372036854775807` holds 2^64-1, the correct value, and prints `-1`, because `FNN64.toString` is signed (`compiler/runtimeValues/FNN64.java:20`; row 326, open, the same situation); `walk` refuses the coercion (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/skeptic/s3.fss`).
113	- The library's scalar extension is eight generic declarations, `opr +[\T extends Number, I\](x: Array[\T,I\], y: T)` and the mirror order, likewise `-`, `MIN` and `MAX` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4720-4730`, `.fsi:2679-2689`), with `Number` closed by its `comprises` clauses (`Number … comprises { RR64, QQ, AnyIntegral }`, `.fss:360-361`; the clause lists `RR32` too, a sibling since it left `RR64`; `AnyIntegral … comprises { ZZ, ZZ64, ZZ32, NN64, NN32 }`, `.fss:655`), `AdditiveGroup` marked by `AnyAdditiveGroup` in the `AnyMultiplicativeRing` pattern (`.fss:336-339`) and `Array3 … excludes { Number, String, AnyAdditiveGroup, AnyMultiplicativeRing }` (`.fss:2851`); it is gated from an empty cache by `ProjectFortress/tests/ArrayScalarExtension.fss` and `ProjectFortress/tests/ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary.fss` with the fixture `ProjectFortress/test_library/ArrayOperatorVocabulary.{fsi,fss}`. A single user declaration of a library operator name behind an api is not checked against the library's, nor is one in a component that only exports it, so exercising the check takes two declarations of one name. `MicroGptFlatCheck` and `MicroGptAplCheck` each run 40 PASS at the first run of an empty cache (rows 341, 342; `run-c4/cold-cache/repair/`).
114	- **A top-level variable imported through an api can be read, assigned and read back on the compiled path** (`compile-ladder/rung-export-var/REPORT.md`). The checker asks the declaring api whether an api-qualified name is mutable (`isMutableName`, `scala_src/typechecker/STypeChecker.scala:345-350`, used at `impls/Operators.scala:444`), and `CodeGen.forVarRef`'s fresh-import path binds a mutable variable to its `MutableFValue` cell (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5985-5998`, `importedVarIsMutable:5960-5967`). Gated by `compiler_tests/ExportVarRungX.test` and, for the immutable refusal, `XXXExportVarRungXFrozen.test`.
115	- Four comments in the interpreter's library record the tower closure's unwritable clause `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:661`, `.fsi:441`; the specification makes that spelling no valid clause and the compiled checker accepts the clause as written, "The tower closure of `02d09a39f` has no spelling the compiler's checker accepts"), the use of rank 3 that `Array3`'s `excludes AnyAdditiveGroup` picks (`.fss:2852-2857`, `.fsi:1799-1804`), that the scalar block's eight return the unsized `Array[\T,I\]` (`.fss:4714-4719`, `.fsi:2673-2678`), and that its reversed `-` is `y - e` elementwise (`.fss:4723-4725`, `.fsi:2682-2684`) (`compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/REPORT.md`).
116	- `round` on a float sends an exact half to the even integer on both paths: `walk`'s `Float$Round` and `RR32$Round` are `(long) Math.rint(…)` (`interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:384`, `RR32.java:326`), as is the compiled `simpleDoubleArith.doubleRound` (`nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java:132-134`); NaN gives 0, values beyond the 64-bit range saturate. Gated by `tests/RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss`; a numeral within half an ulp of a tie is rounded as its nearest double (row 360, `XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss`) (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/REPORT.md`).
117	- A compiled object with no `asString` of its own prints its bare Fortress type name, `walk`'s spelling, through `trait Object`'s default `jDefaultAsString(self)` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:355`) and the native `stringOps.defaultAsString` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/stringOps.java:74-86`); a class with a Java `toString` of its own keeps it. Open: a zero-argument Fortress member named `toString` overflows the stack (row 321, `compiler_tests/XXXFortToStringRungS.test` with `FortToStringRungSLink.test`); rows 363 and 364 (renderings that differ from `walk`) (`compile-ladder/rung-default-rendering/REPORT.md`).
118	- The compiled path's integer rules: `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` on `ZZ32` and `ZZ64` give `0` or the replicated sign at or beyond the width and shift the other way for a negative count (`nativeHelpers/simpleIntArith.java:353-362`, `simpleLongArith.java:322-331`), `<<`, `>>` and `<<<` unchanged; on `ZZ32` and `ZZ64` only the minimum overflows or saturates, and `REM`, `MOD`, `GCD` and `LCM` do not throw on a zero quotient; `ZZ64.narrow` and `NN64.narrow` keep the low 32 bits (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:659`, `:879`) while `asZZ32` throws; `ZZ`'s `<<<` refuses an unrepresentable left shift with a catchable `IntegerOverflow` (`simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.java:93-102`, row 386). Gated by `compiler_tests/IntSemanticsRungB.fss`, `library_tests/IntConversionsRungW.fss` and `tests/FixedWidthOverflowRungB.fss` (`compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-compiled/REPORT.md`).
119	- The interpreter's integer rules: fixed-width `+`, `-`, unary `-`, `|..|`, `DIV` and multiplication raise a catchable `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit ("Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit" below); `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` on the four fixed widths saturate at the width and reverse on a negative count, the count read by its value, `ZZ32`'s taking any `AnyIntegral` count and answering a `ZZ32` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:688-691`, `.fsi:491-492`; POSITIONS, "`LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` are bit operators; `shift` is exact on ℤ"); `ZZ`'s shift is exact (`interpreter/glue/prim/BigNum.java:247`); `GCD` and `LCM` are nonnegative, `0 LCM 0` is `0` (row 385); `LCM`, `CHOOSE` and `^` on the fixed widths raise when the result does not fit, `CHOOSE` answering 0 for `k<0` or `k>n` (row 337); `ZZ64.narrow` keeps the low 32 bits; `shift` on `ZZ` is absent from the compiler prelude (row 383, `compiler_tests/XXXShiftDeclRungI.test`). Gated by `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss` and `PowChooseLcmRungE.fss` (`compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md`, `compile-ladder/rung-shift-count/REPORT.md`).
120	- **What relies on fixed-width wrapping under `walk`, and the wrapping operators no running library declares** (`reviews/wrap-dependent-code.md`, read-only, written before the library declared them): the code that means to wrap, the library's power-of-two range split, `LinearCongruential`, `ChunkedSparseArray` and `IntMap` and six team tests, is spelled with the specification's wrapping operators ∔, ∸ and ⨰ (`opr-overview.tex:172-176`, `:205-209`), which the interpreter's library declares (the sites in "The specification's wrapping operators ∔, ∸ and ⨰ are declared in the interpreter's library" below). They were in the team's 2007 draft library (`0370a14b2`); the compiler prelude declares them with the wraparound and saturating spellings reversed (row 348). `LinearCongruential` (`Library/Random.fss:235`) also gives wrong numbers for any modulus not a power of two. The plain operators raise `IntegerOverflow` on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32` and `NN64` alike, and the three range bodies that answered right at the integer bounds only by wrapping, which no logging pass reached, are rewritten to answer there (row 450; "Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit" below).
121	- **Every functional-method name of the library is reserved in every program that imports it**: the disambiguator's `checkForShadowingVar` (`scala_src/disambiguator/ExprDisambiguator.scala:745-763`) rejects a parameter or local named `even` or `numerator`, "Variable even is already declared.", as the specification forbids a parameter to shadow a functional method within its reach, the whole component and every importer (`Specification/basic/declarations.tex:426-461`, `:533`). So `ZZ`'s `shift(self, k:AnyIntegral): ZZ` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:544`, `.fss:885-886`) came with the library's colliding parameters renamed `amount` (`compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/JUDGE.md`); a `walk` program may not bind `shift`, and the compiled path, with no prelude declaration, keeps no such reservation.
122	- `ProjectFortress/tests/RangePrototype.fss` computes its signed stride as `(this.stride DIV (this.stride GCD other.stride)) DOT other.stride` (`:66`, `:171`), since `LCM` is nonnegative; the library's `RangeInternals.fss` never depended on the sign (`compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md`).
123	- **Under `walk`, the interpreter converts by coercion at its three kinds of type check** (`compile-ladder/rung-interp-coercion/REPORT.md`; for generic declarations `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md`): a parameter of a single function, constructor, method or native (`NonPrimitive.typecheckParams`); an overloaded call when no overload applies without coercion (`OverloadedFunction.bestMatchWithCoercion`, `OverloadedFunction.java:1187`), choosing by `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:477-484`, refusing "Ambiguous coercion" and dispatching the converted call again; a typed binding or assignment (`LHSEvaluator`, `BaseEnv`, `BuildEnvironments`, `LazilyEvaluatedCell`), tuples element by element. The conversions are the lifted `coerce_` functions, chosen on the run-time value (row 389 for a generic trait's), so walk can dispatch plainly where the compiled run converts (POSITIONS, "Walk chooses coercions on the value, for now"; `tests/XXXCoercionStaticRungC.fss`, `XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC.fss`). Not converted: a declared return (row 387), a coercion with its own static parameter (row 513), an overloaded function's tuple parameter or a tuple-typed field (row 395), varargs, keyword and arrow targets. Gated by `tests/CoercionGenericFnRungC.fss`, `CoercionGenericTraitRungC.fss` and `CoercionRedispatchRungC.fss`.

The rule is stated in the Types chapter as a property of exclusion (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:218-237`) and as a rule on declarations (`basic/traits.tex:327-341`); a where-clause variable may not be a static argument in an `extends` clause (`basic/trait-parameters.tex:339-349`). The refused examples are kept marked "Not allowed", each beside the library's shape, which runs on both paths except `Nothing[\String\]` on the compiled prelude (row 331). Each changed passage carries a `\revision` callout, and Appendix I's section "Changes Made by the 2026 Revival to the Working Draft" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, from `:18`) quotes every original and names the cases the checker does not yet refuse (rows 406, 414); the four calculi of Appendix A carry a callout that they predate the rule (`changes.tex:368-434`; POSITIONS, "The refused examples (S2)"). Part IV is rendered from the library's `.fsi` files, so a library api edit changes the PDF there.
159	- **The specification's number chapters describe the flat library, and its advanced chapter on rational quantities is kept word for word as a superseded design** (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/decision-record.md`). ℤ, ℤ64, ℤ32, ℕ64, ℕ32, ℚ, ℝ64 and ℝ32 are siblings under `Number` with the library's coercions, every other conversion explicit, the one into ℝ64 written `asFloat(x)` (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:27-56`, `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:16-37`); the refined types are gone (`numbers.tex:58-72`); ℚ holds +∞, −∞ and 0/0, as `Ratio` does, and claims neither a field nor a total order (`numbers.tex:224-227`). Answer 7's note is a callout at `Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex:27-44`, answer 8's rule, for a generic call only, one at `basic-integers.tex:80-94`; the integer `^` gives no result for a negative power (`:298-320`). Appendix I's I.1.10 to I.1.16 quote every original.
160	- **The specification never wrote static-argument inference or a numeral's type hierarchy, and named a range's integer width only in climb batch 7R** (`reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/evidence-B.md` §§ 1-2, read; `measure-C.md` § 3). The chapter that the overloading rules (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:170-175`), `basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:35-40` and `method-invocation.tex:49-52` cite, `Specification/basic/inference.tex`, is the revival's: it states the rule the checker builds, for type, `nat` and `int` parameters ("The specification's type-inference chapter states the rule of climb batch N" below), and keeps the team's note with its question "Do we want to forbid such cases where type inference infers BottomTypes for static parameters?" (`inference.tex:296-306`); the Working Draft's chapter is 27 lines of heading and notes (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/inference.tex:12-27`). The revival's promotion rule (`basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:90-94`) points to it; `Empty`'s note (`basic/trait-parameters.tex:478-485`, a generic object's static arguments) and the reductions callout (`basic/expressions/reductions.tex:27-44`, a reduction's element type) point into it for cases it names as not described (`inference.tex:237-240`, `:250-251`). A numeral has a type of its own whose relation to the number types is a note ("We need to describe the Numeral type hierarchy", `basic/expressions/literals.tex:87-96`), and "Libraries define coercions from numerals to integers (for simple numerals) and rational numbers (for compound numerals)" (`:146-148`). The coercion chapter defines applicability with coercion by substitutability and names no static parameter (`basic/conversions-coercions.tex:417-432`), states that "types named by type parameters do not have coercions" (`:363-365`), and uses the expected type to re-choose a declaration only in widening (`:820-862`), which is "not yet supported" (`:15`). The Working Draft's ranges section spoke of "integer values" and named no integer type or width (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/ranges.tex:42-44`), while its own examples built `ZZ64` and `ZZ` ranges; the revised section names ℤ32 (`ranges.tex:42-48`; "The specification's ranges are over ℤ32" below). The later restart adds nothing on these: its Types chapter never says "infer" and its ranges section is a heading (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`, `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/Expressions/ranges.tick:12`).
161	- **The specification's ranges are over ℤ32, and its own ranges over wider integer types are respelled** (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-ranges/decision-record.md`). An explicit range's components are ℤ32 values, into which an integer numeral and a `nat` or `int` parameter convert, another integer type is a static error, and a wider counter widens each element (`Specification/basic/expressions/ranges.tex:42-58`, `:88-109`; row 485, closed). The two examples that built `ZZ64` ranges run over ℤ32 (`SpecData/examples/basic/Expr.Do.mySum.fss:19`, `SpecData/examples/advanced/Generators.GeneratorDefn.fss:19-37`), and ℤ's factorial property is stated by recurrence (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:580-590`). Appendix I's I.1.18 and I.1.19 quote every original (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1072-1247`). `ant testSpecData` is not in the gate. Under walk a `nat` parameter in value position is an `Int`, refused at an `NN32` binding (row 486).
162	- **The specification reads a `comprises` clause as the later Types chapter does: every value of the trait is a value of a listed type, and a trait with static parameters may stand unlisted between** (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-comprises/decision-record.md`). Rendered normative text replaces the draft note (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:235-252`): a listed type may be an instantiation over `T`'s static parameters only, so `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]` is no valid clause, and an explicit extender is below a listed type, a closed trait meeting the same requirement, or a trait with static parameters every extender of which is below a listed type. Its callout (`:253-267`) and Appendix I's I.1.20 (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1257-1350`) quote the note; the ellipsis sentence stays in its note (`traits.tex:268-274`); a listed bare type variable is open (row 407); the checker's departures are rows 487, 489 and 490. The four passages that read a clause at the level of types read it at the level of values (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:583-627`, `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:339-372`, `Specification/basic/functions.tex:370-421`, `Specification/basic/components/source-code.tex:428-434`; row 491, fixed), and both paths run the Meet Rule's example (row 492), gated by `tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss` and `compiler_tests/ComprisesMeetCompiled.test`.
163	- **The specification states the integer rules of 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-24, the coercion example with the exclusions its definition needs, and the rational type's library algebra** (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-integer-rules/decision-record.md`). The integer chapter states `narrow`, `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` on the five integer types, `shift` exact at any count, and `GCD` and `LCM` nonnegative (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:39-66`, `:541-568`, `:725-730`); the operator overview, the overflow of a fixed-size result and the shifts among the bitwise operators (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:262-270`, `:341-344`). The coercion chapter's example declares the library's integer exclusions and runs on both paths (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:556-597`; row 394). `QQ`'s listing extends the library's four algebraic traits, their laws holding for the finite rationals (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:224-231`). Appendix I quotes every original (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1352-1557`).
164	- **The specification's type-inference chapter states the rule of climb batch N** (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-inference/decision-record.md`; `compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/REPORT.md` section 1). `Specification/basic/inference.tex:15-294`: the declaration is chosen first, by the coercion chapter's resolution on declared parameter types, so a coercion never changes which declaration is chosen when one applies without it (`:54-63`); then the static arguments, a lone type parameter taking the narrowest of its arguments' types and their coercion targets, otherwise the intersection of its upper bounds, its declared bound (`Any` if none) and what the expected type requires (`:65-124`, `:89-98`), and a type parameter nothing fixes the same intersection, never `BottomType`, in the S1 form (`:99-118`); the expected type with a retry (`:128-154`); a numeral's tie read as ℤ32, ℤ64 or ℤ by value (`:206-229`); what it leaves undescribed (`:231-254`); callouts on the checker (`:26-45`), the interpreter, with walk's departures at dispatch (`:169-204`; rows 588, 589, 591), and the bound, a reduction's big operator and walk's instances, with the parameters walk leaves at `BottomType` (`:255-294`; rows 424, 587, 591, 592). Appendix I's I.1.25 quotes every original, names the five cases, rows 508, 515, 516, 518 and 541, in which the checker departed from the chapter, in each of which it follows it, and gives walk's departures, four kinds by decision and three as defects (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1559-1885`, `:1792-1808`, `:1705-1736`). Against the checker (the decision record, section 6; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/RECORD.md`, rung T) every statement holds except 4 for `ZZ32` with `NN32` on the compiler prelude (row 442); 12, at `f(x)` and at an operator, holds (row 508; POSITIONS, "The order of the checker's attempts at a call"), and 5 holds on both paths, walk's except for a lone parameter whose bound mentions a static parameter or that is declared with several bounds walk cannot meet (rows 515, 516 and 591; POSITIONS, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix takes its bound, never `Bottom`"), gated by `compiler_tests/InferLoneBound`, `InferLoneUnbounded`, `tests/InferLoneBoundWalk.fss` and `InferLoneUnboundedWalk.fss`.
165	- **The specification states the type group's 2011 overloading model: declarations of one name may differ in their static parameters, and a declaration with static parameters is read over its instances** (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-overloading/decision-record.md`; POSITIONS, "The static-parameter sentence goes"). The Working Draft's sentence and its echo are replaced (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-120`, `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:109-123`); a declaration with static parameters is applicable when some instance within its bounds is, compared on its declared parameter types (`basic/overloading.tex:149-159`, `:194-205`, `:235-242`, `:365-375`). "Declarations with Static Parameters" (`advanced/overloading.tex:531-651`) states the paper's three rules, with the positional rule in a callout as the compiled implementation's restriction; neither implementation runs the paper's repair (rows 159, 537). The coercion chapter cross-references it and carries the callout on walk's choice of a coercion on the value (`basic/conversions-coercions.tex:663-675`). The implicit bound is `Any` (`basic/trait-parameters.tex:49-62`; row 412); the naked-`Any` rule is against a written `Any`, as `OverloadingChecker.checkBoundAny` applies it (`scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:430-439`; row 534). Appendix I's seven entries name the departures (rows 159, 537, 539, 542). The specification builds at 655 pages with no undefined reference (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/RECORD.md`, "The landing").
166	- **The specification gives the run-time instance of a dispatched declaration by the POPL 2019 paper's rule, a lone type parameter with no narrowest candidate its bound, and reads a `comprises` clause at the level of values in every passage** (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-overloading/decision-record.md`; POSITIONS, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix takes its bound, never `Bottom` (the paper's instance rule)." and "The `comprises` passages read at the level of values (PLAN item 26, row 491)"). The dispatch paragraph (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:312-332`): the declaration the static call selected runs at its inferred instance, any other at the intersection of its upper bounds, fixed by the value at an invariant position, never `BottomType` nor the union; its callout (`:333-349`) says both implementations take the value's type (row 538, `compiler_tests/XXXGenericInstanceUnfixed`). The inference chapter gives a lone type parameter with no narrowest candidate its bound (`basic/inference.tex:89-98`), its Appendix I entry listing the checker's departures (rows 508, 515, 516, 518, 541). Under item 26 covering is defined (`basic/types-vals-vars.tex:590-601`), the Meet Rule has its closed-trait case for functions and functional methods, a call between two closed traits is typed by the meet of its candidates' return types where none has static parameters (rows 540, 543, 546, 547), and the proof appendix marks row 487's closure assumption (`Specification/appendices/overloading-function.tex`).
167	- **The specification allows arithmetic in a size and does not say when two size expressions are the same type** (`Specification/appendices/grammars/concrete-syntax.tex:533-547`, `:675-681`; `Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:15-24`, `:70-71`; `Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:49-52`; `Specification/appendices/internal-document.tex:167-199`). A static argument may be a numeral, a name, a sum, a difference, a product, a power with a numeral or a bracketed expression, and denotes its number, marked by the team "not yet supported"; types are identical when their static arguments are "identical", beside the team's note "It isn't complete in any case", and the 2012 Types chapter drops the sentence; the team's Q&A refuses `T[\n+1\]` beside `T[\0\]`. The compiled checker refuses any arithmetic in a size (`scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:41-47`, `:84`) and compares sizes as different (`Formula.scala:100-105`); walk computes `+`, `-` and juxtaposition at instantiation (`interpreter/evaluator/EvalType.java:467-479`) and binds only a name or a numeral at a call (`types/IntNat.java:133-146`); the compiled name mangler spells the expression out (`NamingCzar.java:1899-1905`). PLAN item 15 holds the two routes.
168	## The territory map
169	
170	- Tasks and transactions are implemented twice, `interpreter/evaluator/` and `runtimeSystem/`, independently (B.11). Row 302's fix is in the compiled world's copy only.
171	- `import java` works on the interpreter path through `ForeignComponentWrapper` + `ClosureMaker`, as `map/modules-and-phases.md:451` (B.12) reads it, once six small Java patches close its five gaps, and one binding text then serves both paths (2026-09-29, `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape.md` § 1, programs, patches and captures under `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape/`, a classpath shadow and private caches at `f55fd68e2`; the first four gaps were found by `perf-probes/prelude/import-java-interpreter.md`, which changed no Java). On the tree it is wired and unfinished, and no test uses it. A two-declaration `import java` component in `CompilerBuiltin.fss`'s shape, one `import java` line per helper class from one package, runs on walk under the six patches, +120 −20 lines of Java in six files, one of them new, and prints what the compiled path prints, for top-level functions and for a trait's functional method and an object's dotted method alike; the interpreter suite, what `ant testSystem` runs, is green under them (`testFast` not run). The gaps, in the order a program meets them: (1) `NamingCzar`'s foreign-type table places every Java type in the builtin api (`NamingCzar.java:294-295`, `:436-450`), which in walk's world declares none of `ZZ32`, `RR64` and `JavaString`; the probe's patch (+14 −11) is a device, since at the switch-over the table names the one library's types for both paths; (2) a second `import java` from one package ends in a `ClassCastException` at `Driver.java:468` ("temp hack till we knit in natives properly"), whose two callers do not read the value (+2 −2); (3) the foreign name keeps the unset depth, "Non-top-level reference to imported …" (`interpreter/evaluator/BaseEnv.java:535-537`), and the cure is the reference's depth, the top level for an api-qualified reference as the desugarer already sets it for an api-qualified type name (`interpreter/rewrite/DesugarerVisitor.java:694-697`, +3), not filling `ForeignComponentWrapper`'s rewrite map; (4) `ClosureMaker` emits a call into the compiler's `nativewrapper_cache`, which walk neither writes nor loads, replaced by a closure that calls the helper by reflection, unboxing each argument and boxing the result by its Java type (the new `interpreter/glue/ForeignNativeApp.java` and `ClosureMaker.java:119-141`, +71 −6), with its parameter types finished after `initTypes` (`Driver.java:224-226`, +17 −1); (5) a helper raises a Fortress exception by naming a class of the compiled prelude, `Utility.makeFortressException("fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IntegerOverflow")` (`compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:45-58`), at 55 sites (`IntegerOverflow` 37, `DivisionByZero` 16, `FileNotFoundException` 2), which walk ends as a `FortressImplementationError` until the raise is translated into walk's own raise of the library object of that name (+13). `ForeignNativeApp` converts `int`, `long`, `double`, `float`, `boolean`, `String` and `BigInteger`; helpers over compiled-world types (`fortress.AnyType$Any`, `CompilerBuiltin$IntLiteral`, `FortressBufferedReader` and `Writer`, `FZZ32Vector` and `FStringVector`, 50 parameters or results) cannot take walk's values, and walk's speed through a reflective call is not measured. The library's own construct can be the one text instead: a `builtinPrimitive("…")` string naming a static helper runs under walk with a 72-line loader (`patches/opt1-builtinprimitive-static.patch`, a fallback in `NativeApp.java:196` and the new `StaticNativeApp.java`), the suite green under it; its compiled half, a front-end rewrite of each such body through the `import java` machinery, is not measured (one to two rungs by reading). The shape of one api with a builtin component per path is not needed, and with it neither is ledger row 320's linker step (`Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`, `linker/Linker.java:72-76`), which would not reach the bindings inside `FortressLibrary.fss` itself nor those of `FlatString`, `Writer` and `NativeArray`. Which construct is the one binding text is PLAN item 35, for Pavol; the bindings, counted and classed, are the first entry of "The checker and the one library".
172	- Codegen refuses any declaration carrying a where clause or a contract (`CodeGen.java:2953`/`:2957` in `forFnDecl`, `:4093`/`:4095` in `forObjectDeclPrePass`, `:5004`/`:5006` in `forTraitDecl`); not in the ledger (flagged, Pavol's call). `atomic <expr>` has no visitor, `atomic do … end` compiles; `spawn`, `label`/`exit`, object expressions, array literals and comprehensions, local function declarations have no visitor (`spec-to-implementation.md` §3).
173	- The checker (`IndexBuilder.scala:187-189`) refuses `type` aliases, `test` and `property` on both paths. Coercion, which the compiler path had and the interpreter did not (row 19), converts on both paths ("Under `walk`, the interpreter converts by coercion at its three kinds of type check" under Landed semantics).
174	- **The compiled path's only array-like types are `ZZ32Vector` and `StringVector`, two hand-written Java classes declared only in its prelude and absent from the specification** (`compiler-probes/vectors/vectors.md`, probes and captures under `compiler-probes/vectors/probes/`). `FZZ32Vector` holds an unboxed `int[]` with lower bounds and an optional second dimension (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ32Vector.java:14-19`), `FStringVector` a `String[]`; `NamingCzar`'s special table lowers both types straight to the classes (`compiler/NamingCzar.java:553-554`); every element access is boxed and passes through seven frames, a generated native wrapper among them; no gated test creates or indexes a `ZZ32Vector` at run time. The load failure of a `ZZ32Vector` passed to a generic object's constructor (ledger row 408, expected failure `compiler_tests/XXXVecCtorLoad`) is the descriptor class's name: both classes call it `RTTIv` (`FZZ32Vector.java:79-82`) while stamped code asks for `<class>$RTTIc` (`runtimeSystem/MethodInstantiater.java:134-138`), and a probe-only copy with an `RTTIc` alias runs (`probes/rttic-alias.patch`, `out-VecGeneric-rttic.txt`). A native helper cannot take a Java array: the wrapper generator skips every method with an array parameter (`compiler/nativeInterface/SignatureParser.java:45-55`). Written by Christine Flood (`f4973a717`, `24717d4ad`) and extended by Guy Steele (`d535963cb`).
175	- **A generic object referenced without its static arguments is a static error on the compiled path, and the checker never consults the expected type for it** (`explorations/compiler-probes/maybe-inference/inference.md`): `b: Box[\ZZ32\] = Box` fails with `Ill-formed type: Box`; a bare `Empty` as a call argument or a field default fails with `T is not in the kind env`, an internal `bug()` from `TypeAnalyzer.scala:766` reported at the declaration's span; the same forms with the static argument written compile and run on both paths. The decision is in the checker's `SVarRef` case, `typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:624-641`, whose `:639-640` keeps the uninstantiated type under the team's own `TODO: handle missing static args`; static-argument inference exists only for arrows (`STypesUtil.scala:912-930`, called from application and coercion), and a parametric empty case reached by `coerce` still fails bare; the inference chapter names a generic object named without a call as not described. Under `walk` the same forms are `InterpreterBug: Couldn't figure out Empty[\T\](uninstantiated) <: Opt[\ZZ32\]`. Consequence for row 331: a parametric `Nothing[\T\]` would serve the corpus's `Nothing[\ZZ32\]` and never the specification's bare `= Nothing`; the non-parametric object plus `coerce` that the prelude uses is the only shape that compiles, so `Maybe` stays as landed. Incidental, row 340: a `typecase` used directly as a function or method body whose value needs an implicit coercion (`IntLiteral` to a declared `ZZ32`) crashes code generation with `Error trying to close method scope`, because ASM's stack-map frame computation fails (`ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` under `MethodWriter.visitMaxs`, relabelled by the `catch (Throwable)` at `CodeGen.java:2806-2807`); neither a generic object nor `typecase` alone is the trigger (the minimal reproducer, `compiler-probes/maybe-inference/probes/TcPlain.fss`); wrapped in `do … end` the same body compiles, and every gated use of the shape returns `()` so never reaches the coercion.
176	- The gate: two corpora, hand-ported: `tests/` shares no file name with `compiler_tests/`, and the 11 names it shares with `other_compiler_tests/` are different programs; only `parser_tests/` is read by both suites, and no test compares the paths on one program (`map/README.md`); interpreter tests pass on "no exception and no `fail` in output" (`FileTests.java:382-386`), compiler run tests on exit code plus `PASS`. `fortress.unittests.noopt=true` (`default_repository/configuration:51`) hides 283 tests and leaves the 43-file bytecode optimizer with zero (`map/README.md`). Every `testSystem` shard and every `testFast` fork runs `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` (`build.xml:1188`, `:947`), so no suite test sees concurrency and the gate's four-thread `atomic` runs are its one concurrent check; `TransactionJUTest`'s multi-threaded half is commented out (`TestTask.java:43-44`). `nat`-parameterised programs are compiled and run (`compiler_tests/Nat*`); the cache round trip is not asserted (`ASTJUTest.java:654`). 121 `.fss` inside green directories are dark; `linker_tests`, `compiler_regressions`, `BirdyLib`, the `not_working_*` directories are orphaned (`map/test-coverage.md`).
177	
178	## The container
179	
180	- The process cost of the climbs and the batches — the eight-rung climb's wall clock and its gate share, the limits of parallelism on this box, and each batch's agents, tokens, tool calls and span — is measured in `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md`, `coordinator/repair-batch-review.md` and the batch records; `postmortem-2026-09-29/characterization.md` measures every batch's token spend by stage; the conclusions it produced are in `POSITIONS.md` and in `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js`, and the entries themselves are in `FACTS-history.md`.
181	- **A boot after a compaction costs about 285K tokens of context, and `FACTS.md` is about two fifths of it** does not hold: a boot costs about 250K of context, and `FACTS.md` is about a third of it (session `fe616d40`'s main transcript, each read's tokens the growth of the next call's prompt). The first call after the compaction is about 74K: the fixed part (system prompt, tools, skills, memory), about 56K read from the cache, and the compaction summary with the text the harness re-injects after it, about 18K written. The boot's reads then add `FACTS.md` about 88K (220 KB, read in five pages of about 45 KB, since the Read tool's page holds 25K tokens), `INDEX.md` 45K, `POSITIONS.md` 22K, the README and the protocol about 6K, and the handover's first section and the boot note about 14K; while a batch runs, its record's sections for Pavol and its journal add about 14K. Every read is written to the cache, so a boot writes about 195K, about 210K while a batch runs. A read costs about 2.5 bytes of file per token for `FACTS.md`, 2.7 for `INDEX.md` and 3.0 for `POSITIONS.md`, denser than prose because of paths, line numbers and code, so an estimate of a boot from file sizes uses these figures. `/context` shows the last call's prompt plus about 0.5K.
182	- The Bash tool's 10-minute ceiling kills long runs; check runs go under the `Monitor` tool (1800000 ms), sequential, nothing else running when a number is to be kept.

The runs the cap ended are all of nearly the same length, 46,636 to 46,660 s (12 h 57 min 16 s to 12 h 57 min 49 s); the rest are short runs of a few minutes to a few hours that end when the session goes idle, and VM restarts. The cap's stops are not a crash, not memory and not a message; they fall while Pavol is talking because the process runs continuously only while he or a check-in keeps it busy. Any restart, a VM start included, resets the clock, so the next stop is the last start plus 12 h 58 min, and a check-in armed a few minutes after that time resumes what the stop killed; the last start and the next stop are the boot note's.
- **`explorations/experiment/env.sh` is the one script every probe and gate runner sources, and it is verified from its new home** (after `experiment/` moved under `explorations/`): it derives `FORTRESS_HOME` from its own location two levels up, and re-running the two shadow experiments that source it, `reviews/mie-probes/forest/forest-run.sh` (423 s) and `perf-probes/nat/runtime/run-all.sh` (669 s), reproduced every committed count and probe output (`checker-count.txt`'s six counts, stock 103 and forest 37 among them, and captures r1-r5 byte-identical); the only differences were dates, timings and line numbers shifted by later library commits. The separate analysis session's scripts keep their own `experiment/` paths, which name that session's tree.
- **An agent that waits longer than the prompt cache lives writes its whole context again at every wake** (session `fe616d40`, `subagents/agent-af9b2c3ba93eb9c88.jsonl`, probe P1's worker, its usage records deduplicated by message id). Of the 7.0M P1's worker wrote in 263 calls, 6.6M were 19 calls that each wrote 240K to 330K, its whole context, with no cache read, every one after a wait of 8 to 13 minutes on a build or a run; between waits its calls read the cache. The cache's life is in the API's usage records: every cache write of the main session is labelled one hour (`cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`) and every subagent's five minutes (`ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`), as the platform's own description of the main session's wake-ups says of the main session. A poll within the life reads the cache and renews it, so a wait in steps costs a cache read per step. A workflow agent's waits are capped at 270 s for this reason (`wait_for` in `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js`); an `Agent`-tool worker's brief carries the same cap, its long run polled in steps under 270 s, or the run handed to a script while the agent ends its turn.
- **A check-in cadence under an hour is a series of one-shot `send_later` check-ins armed together in one turn, not a cron trigger and not a re-armed one-shot** (a worker's search of session `fe616d40`'s main transcript at Pavol's request). The scheduler's cron triggers take an hour as their shortest interval. Seven `send_later` calls in one turn, each `{"at": ..., "name": "Batch 5 check-in N", "message": ...}` 45 minutes apart, fired within a minute of each target, with no re-arming; a series 90 minutes apart and a chain of one `send_later` per check-in, each re-issued by the turn it started, are the other forms tried. The scheduler refuses more than about ten trigger creations a minute: the eleventh `send_later` of a series got "Trigger creation rate limit reached. Try again in 56s." A series ends when its last check-in has fired, so a run that outlasts it needs a new series, armed by the last check-in. The cadence is 45 minutes (POSITIONS, "Check-ins and stops").
- **`agent()` in a Workflow returns null for an agent the harness marks failed, even after the agent delivered its structured output** (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "An agent that comes back with nothing"). A second skeptic returned its verdict, an approval with one required correction, through the structured-output tool; the API's safety filter then blocked its next message, a false-positive `reasoning_extraction` refusal, and the harness marked the agent failed (the run's `journal.jsonl`, `"type":"failed"`). `agent()` returned null, and the script recorded the rung as `dropped`, although that approval was committed on the rung's `wip/` branch. Every `agent()` call of the batch script goes through `callAgent`, which treats a null or undefined result and a thrown error alike and runs the role up to two more times, each retry told what the earlier attempt may have left (`ATTEMPTS` and `callAgent` in `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js`, the retry's head written by `retryHead` from the stage's `recover…` list).
- **`node --check` does not check the batch script as the Workflow harness parses it, so a spliced script is checked by parsing it as an async function body** (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`). Two unescaped apostrophes inside a single-quoted string of `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` once passed `node --check` and were refused by the Workflow parser at launch; the harness runs the script as a function body. On this container's Node, v22.22.2, `node --check` exits 0 on a two-line file holding `export const meta = {}` and the same slip and refuses the slip alone. The check that catches it: the script's text, with `export const meta` made `const meta`, handed to `new AsyncFunction(...)` (`AsyncFunction` being `Object.getPrototypeOf(async function(){}).constructor`), which throws "Unexpected identifier 's'" on the slip and accepts the script without it.
- **The session's automatic permission check refuses a step that lands work on an earlier gate than the one the record names, even after Pavol's go in chat, and his switch to manual approval is the way through** (session `fe616d40`). In auto mode it refused twice to move a gate's earlier outputs (`tmp/gate-batch-N.prev-0653`) back over a later, stopped run's, after Pavol's "Land on the first gate.", and then refused a change to a check-in trigger's prompt that would have done the same, naming it an auto-mode bypass; its rule is that a refused outcome is not pursued by another tool or a later turn. Pavol switched the session to manual approval, the move then ran with no prompt at all, and he switched back to auto after the launch. A `/permissions` allow rule for the command is the other way he has. In manual mode a Workflow agent's commands wait for his approval: a gate judge once waited on one prompt for 29 minutes, the gap in its transcript; auto mode lets a batch run unattended. The check also refused a check-in trigger whose prompt would turn the platform's git-check Stop hook off again after a restart ("Logging/Audit Tampering", the coordinator's log), and that outcome is not pursued (the transcript backup's entry above; `coordinator/remote-container.md` § How the snapshot works).
- **The push loop pushes `main` every 4 minutes when every unpushed commit touches only `explorations/`, and otherwise only the backup branch `wip/main-backup`, so that a container loss loses nothing and `main` stays gated** does not hold: no push loop runs, and the coordinator pushes `main` and `claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8` itself after every commit. The loop's script is `scratchpad/autopush.sh` in the session's scratchpad, its log `scratchpad/autopush.log`; its fallback branch `wip/main-backup`, which took the commits that touched paths outside `explorations/` so that `main` stayed gated, held nothing that `main` does not and is deleted from the remote with the other `wip/` branches but the last batch's rung branches (`coordinator/PLAN.md`, the housekeeping item under "Off the path, parked").
