1	<!-- What Pavol has decided, holds or already knows, as it stands now: each position in plain words, what we do and why, under a bold title that is its handle; a quote only where his words are the position itself. Timeless: no dates, no provenance, no account of how a position was reached. That record is `POSITIONS-history.md`, where every earlier text of every entry stands verbatim with what became of it. A position he has replaced is gone from here and the later one stands; a decision not yet built keeps the detail the coming work needs. A worker or a coordinator may add an entry with a date or a quote in it; the next consolidation compiles that out into the history and leaves the position. Standing directives about how we work are in `explorations/protocol.md`, and what is established is in `FACTS.md`; neither is repeated here. Read whole at session start, so that none of it is re-asked or re-explained. -->
2	
3	# Pavol's positions, decisions and known ground
4	
5	## The goal
6	
7	- **The measuring stick.** Finish what the designers intended, judged by the specification in `Specification/`, the Working Draft of 2010-12 as the revival revises it, with the 2012 Types chapter cited beside it; not redesign the language. The measure is one program, microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast. A pure-Java microGPT is written later as the floor to measure against. The specification is a living document that reflects the changes we make. The tree is tagged `sealed-tree` at the map's last commit; commits after it edit the original sources, test-driven.
8	- **How he weighs his calls where the designers left no word.** "I don't care about type theoretical purity and I'm accepting all unfinished corners of the language because I want to get to a compiled version of micro GPT. And I think this is the right pragmatic approach so that we do not get bogged down in weeds. Theory. We want to get this one program running fast. That's our guiding star. But along the way, I want to stay true to the spirit of Fortress." He has not read the specification, the papers on its type system or the library, and relies on the record: "I assume those people knew much more than I do right now." The check he asked for is a thorough top-tier review of every decision of his against the designers' intent, for errors of commission and of omission (`reviews/decisions-review/evidence.md`, `judgement.md`, `popl-recheck.md`); its items are decisions below.
9	- **The readable expression.** The toy problem is microGPT and the search is for its most readable expression: "we are searching for the optimal expression of the microGPT algorithm for readability." Fortress's mathematical notation and Iverson's APL notation (with Hsu's data design for data-flow algorithms) are the two sources. The Hsu-style flat program gave "a few lumps of coal", not a diamond; the vocabulary is where any polishing happens. C4 is the APL target form; C2's tuple hyperparameter form is what a strand assignment expands to; the semicolon form is set aside.
10	- **The APL side quest is closed.** It was a curiosity, then a ladder to learn APL, then native code (not an interpreter in an interpreter) with microGPT as its target; its remaining ground (tacit, characters, nested arrays) is not pursued.
11	- **The 2D notation is a gimmick.** Fortify's mathematical rendering is "a neat gimmick, not a good idea": it encodes one perspective on a computation into the syntax, while the same mathematics can be written many ways; APL's glyph-per-transformation is the purer realisation. Presentation only, not on the path, not an argument for Fortress; no work on it unless he asks.
12	- **The type checker on interpreter programs.** He wants the checker, which runs only on the compile path, usable on interpreter programs, and considers it low-hanging fruit. It comes after the switch-over, when walk also takes the static coercions the checker inserts (the entry on walk's choice of coercions).
13	
14	## History he knows (do not re-explain)
15	
16	- **The project's end.** DARPA's HPCS did not take Sun into phase three (2006) and the project lived on at Sun Labs until 2012. His reading: they did no work on performance, "mucked around with syntax", and the promise that a sufficiently advanced compiler would later make mathematical types fast was never true; the funding was pulled for good reason.
17	- **Boxed numerics.** The compiled path is only about ten times the interpreter because numerics are boxed (`FRR64`, no `DADD`); "without unboxed doubles and arrays of doubles, what are we even doing here". The first measurement's scalar loop was an edge case microGPT never hits (literals in the loop, a `:=` accumulator); the fairer test he asked for agreed with him (FACTS § Execution model). The storage is his decision below; unboxed arithmetic is phase 6 of the plan.
18	- **Hsu's critique** of language paradigms as accidental complexity; he is "coming around to his point of view".
19	- **The third-party Java 9 port** gets no credit and no mention: "I don't wanna see them mentioned anywhere." CLAUDE.md no longer describes the tree as the port's migration grafted on the history; the other files that repeat that sentence wait for the lineage cleanup (`PLAN.md`). His plan to rename the graft-free `clean-ladder` branch to `main` was not carried out.
20	
21	## Decisions on record
22	
23	### The standard and the sources
24	
25	- **The specification stays the standard, the Types chapter beside it.** Where the Types chapter of the team's unfinished restart (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`) covers a topic, it is cited beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word: the exclusion rule as "instantiation exclusion" in its two-part form, the `covariant` modifier, `Bottom` inexpressible. "On the rule S revises, it is the designers' latest intent, and the goal is to finish what they intended."
26	- **The type group's late positions outweigh the early text.** The specification "was written in a vacuum early on", "as a wish"; "then the type group went in and tried to make it run. So they knew much more about what's feasible and what's not. The goal was performance. The specialization is a must"; "when that wish met reality, then the spec must change"; "whatever the spec was dreaming about in 2008 is irrelevant because it met hard reality". So the late, implementation-informed positions of the type group (the exclusion rule, specialization kept, the compiled tower flattened by Steele in 2011, Naden's 2012 write-up, the POPL 2019 paper) outweigh the specification's earlier text where they conflict, and the implementers' later word outweighs unfinished text. "We are not Naden. We know nothing here."
27	- **The library's own practice is the standard.** "all the extensions that [microGPT] invented need to go directly to the standard library in the spirit of the standard library." Exclusion "is a practice that is all over the standard library"; whoever extends the library "should study the existing parts of the Fortress library meticulously, and use those patterns for extending the standard library in the native way". No fix is designed from a reading of the specification alone or from a user-side workaround. A fork put to him names the library's own way first, and a fork resting on a rule that refuses something says what the library does instead (protocol principle 2). The lesson behind the rule: he had to find the diagonal's override shape himself ("why the fuck did I have to invent this solution?"), because the step skipped was what the library already does in the same family.
28	- **Fleshing out the standard library** is a very important task: first the `RR64`/`AdditiveGroup` mismatch (done by the flattening), then the algebraic layer (Ring, Field and what ML's matrices and tensors need) so the library's trait flavour reaches them; into the standard library itself, not a tree of our own.
29	- **Interpreter performance is irrelevant.** "interpreter of Fortress, which is hundreds times slower than the Python interpreter, is irrelevant for any performance discussions"; "we cannot judge anything performance related in Fortress while we do not have a compiler". No edit to C4 for speed, and no performance decision of any kind until microGPT runs compiled. The two microGPT programs never run in the gate ("those are too long running to be tests"); the ladder-regression stage compiles them and records the phase; when they one day run, the run goes to a separate non-gating stage.
30	- **Development-loop performance is a first-class concern.** When an iteration waits too long on something, find the cause and fix it.
31	- **The territory map** (`coordinator/map/`) is the map down to where the design intent is written, papers as well as the specification; he wanted it before unsealing. The maps exist so that nothing on record is rediscovered; the boot order is followed as written, `INDEX.md` included.
32	- **The plan** (`coordinator/PLAN.md`) is six phases, approved with its workers: 1, the wrapping operators, the specification rung without the number chapters and the run-time size rung; 2, the flattening, the number chapters and the overflow natives; 3, the checker at a true zero; 4, the switch-over, natives then names; 5, microGPT compiles: its static types, the array design and the code-generation holes; 6, microGPT fast. Phases 1 and 2 are landed. His answers come in the plan's order; the re-approval rows and the other off-path items are parked until relevant; row 41 joins the switch-over's design.
33	
34	### The one library and the compiled checker
35	
36	- **The library route.** "we need to unify this. into single library"; "the compiler second library is just a bootstrap and we need to get rid of it." One library, the interpreter's (`FortressLibrary` + `FortressBuiltin`), becomes the library the compiler checks; no declaration goes into the compiler's prelude (`CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerAlgebra`); the prelude-name rungs of the ladder stopped, code-generator rungs continue; the three prelude files are deleted at the switch-over and their tests kept. How the checker is brought to accept the library is a plan put to him step by step, not a decision to re-ask.
37	- **The compiler prelude's leftovers go at the switch-over.** The compiler-prelude block for `Maybe` stands as landed, its tests kept, its lines gone then; the guard `if other = -1 then 0` in the two compiled `REM` bodies (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:601`, `:686`) stays and goes with the prelude; the prelude's reversed spellings of the wrapping and saturating operators (row 348) are respelled then, in 10 compiled test files; `ZZ64`'s compiled shift declaration (row 381) closes when the compiled path reads this library; the specification's `shift` (row 383) reaches the compiled path then, `compiler_tests/XXXShiftDeclRungI.test` promoted and `shift` a reserved name on the compiled path from then on, the switch-over batch measuring which compiler tests bind it.
38	- **The checker count is measured, never red.** The checker-count stage stays in every gate, reported and never red on its own; the full distance measurement (all apis and components) is a report-only stage of the phase-3 gates, whose job is driving it down.
39	- **Sizes.** The checker checks `nat` and `int` parameters (built). A size left unknown after inference is an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value, and nothing otherwise ("the middle is a clear winner"); how the checker represents an unknown size was not his to decide. Deleting the dead sizes (E3, 25 api declarations) is shown to him as a diff with the switch-over's design, with row 41. Every static argument counts in the exclusion rule except operator arguments ("sizes count"); booleans follow once the checker supports boolean parameters (row 406). A size the call cannot fix is an error at that call, also inside overload sets: when the arm the rules would pick has a size the call cannot fix, the call is refused with the same "could not infer" error instead of the arm being dropped (row 400 closed). A `nat` parameter is an `NN32` value and an `int` parameter a `ZZ32` (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:82-90`); a larger one is refused; the array design refuses a JVM array length over 2^31-1 where it makes storage ("that's not even a question"). A size used as a value converts to `ZZ32` as a numeral does (row 485); sizes as `NN32` and ranges as `ZZ32` are consistent, since array lengths and indices are Java `int`, a size is never negative and ranges count through negatives. All built.
40	- **The run-time size design is B.** A size at run time gets the same descriptor object a type argument has, filling the slot the team's code generator reserved ("of course, let's extend the runtime object with a new field for the size"); one descriptor per number from a table, no holder class, the team's instantiation pattern applied to numbers. Operators are not unified with the descriptor-bearing kinds ("I don't see a need"). Built.
41	- **The implicit bound of an unbounded type parameter is `Any`**, the top, holding tuples, functions and `()`, which `Object` does not; the library's generic containers are instantiated at tuples, arrays indexed by pairs among them. The specification states it (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:49-62`), with a callout recording the Working Draft's `Object` (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/trait-parameters.tex:49-50`) and naming the compile path's `Object` setting (row 412) as the divergence until the switch-over.
42	- **The exclusion rule stays and the tower is flat (route A).** "Agreed. Route A it is." The compiled checker keeps the multiple instantiation exclusion rule; the library's numeric tower is flattened as Steele flattened the compiler prelude in 2011: the fixed widths, `ZZ`, `QQ` and `RR64` siblings under `Number`, each carrying its own algebra, `Number` without its catch-all operators, a `coerce` on each wider type converting from the narrower; the interpreter converts by coercion at dispatch; the specification is revised with a decision record that preserves the original text, the reasoning and route C. ℤ sits inside ℚ by coercion. Built. Reversal to route C costs what FACTS's route C entry lists. His readings while the fork was open stand: the patents' forest rule against the flattened prelude was "the team's last record on how to do the 'Fortress' way", the route culminating in the POPL 2019 paper, which keeps the rule and specialisation by a run-time return-type check; and "without specialized code there will be no change at performance. But how a specialization is chosen 'ist mir egal', as long as it runs fast."
43	- **`AnyIntegral`'s closure and how the checker reads `comprises`.** The generic scalar-extension block with its two unnamed choices, the `AnyAdditiveGroup` marker and the `Array3` exclusion stand as landed, and so does the closure `AnyIntegral comprises { ... }`, with a `NOT YET`-style comment in the team's wording at the line. The checker reads a `comprises` clause the 2012 way (the later Types chapter, `types.tick:384-389`, and Welterweight): a generic child of a closed trait is eligible when every type the checker knows under it is listed (`everyKnownSubtypeListed`), with an S1 callout in `Specification/basic/traits.tex`; the clause and walk stay as they are; a ledger row records the hole every way but the 2008 clause shares (a program's own `Integral` subtype in another component is not caught). Built. Of the api's overloading and return-type errors this let through, answer 9's families are repaired by the library's own exclusions, `seq`'s remaining pairs aside (FACTS, "The one library's refused overload families are repaired by its own exclusions ..."), and the meet rule and the residue are batch 8's.
44	- **The static-parameter sentence goes (answer 9).** The specification's sentence that overloads may not differ in static parameters is dropped; the specification is revised to the type group's 2011 model the checker runs, the original kept as superseded text in the S1 form. The checker keeps the paper's three rules with two changes: the return-type rule is checked over every instance, and one narrow rule stays, that two generic arms in the more-specific relation agree on their static parameters position by position (Java's overriding rule; it closes row 398). Walk dispatches by declared domains, which ends its dependence on declaration order. The library's refused families are repaired by its own devices. No model line changes. Built: the specification states the 2011 model; the checker checks the return-type rule over every instance, and the positional rule, return-type condition only, for two declarations with as many static parameters of their own, the scope listed for his review; walk chooses by declared domains; the library's families are repaired by its own exclusions but for `seq`'s remaining pairs (FACTS, "The specification states the type group's 2011 overloading model ...", "The compiled checker checks the Return Type Rule over every instance and answer 9's positional rule", "Walk chooses between a generic declaration and another on their declared domains ..." and "The one library's refused overload families are repaired by its own exclusions ..."). The judgement's section 10 items (walk and an unused unknown size, `seq`'s device, Naden's instantiation) took the record's defaults, listed for his review, and what the build left open for him is listed in `PLAN.md` beside them.
45	- **Conversions never change which declaration runs.** A conversion is applied to make a call possible and never changes which declaration runs when one already fits; declarations are chosen by the coercion chapter's order, applicability and specificity taken on declared, quantified domains as answer 9 words them (a generic declaration fits when some instance within its bound fits); the chosen declaration is then instantiated by answer 8's promotion, its coercions inserted statically, and the rewritten call dispatches on the converted values; a numeral whose candidate types are incomparable reads as `ZZ32` (`ZZ64` or `ZZ` by magnitude), stated once in the inference chapter. So a generic arm over `T extends Number` beside a plain arm over `Any` runs the generic at `ZZ64` for a mixed-width call, the specialised instance; plain declarations are untouched; the broader rule (his own idea, "if there is a conversion to a specific type, it should be applied. And only if all combinations are exhausted and we haven't reached a specific implementation, then we go to a plain implementation") is not taken. His principle behind it: "we must make it fast, and generic is never fast. So make it fast." — fast code a JVM can specialise. With it, the inference rule: the checker infers a static argument with coercion, answer 8's promotion its number case, and keeps the expected type at a call written `f(x)` with a retry without it, so that a binding's coercion still applies; walk does the same at dispatch, re-instantiating the chosen declaration by the promotion from run-time types; the specification's type-inference chapter states it in the S1 form. Built: the checker and walk infer as stated, walk dispatching a converted call again (FACTS, "Walk chooses between a generic declaration and another on their declared domains ..."); the numeral tie rule is stated once, in the inference chapter; the stock compiled crash is a row closed by a test (row 504); the two-generic dispatcher defect is gated for phase 5 (row 537).
46	- **Each integer type declares its own `MIN`, `MAX` and `MINMAX`** (row 484), as `QQ`, `RR64`, the compiler library and the specification's `ZZ` do, so under walk the family answers at the promoted type. Built.
47	- **A type parameter the arguments do not fix takes its bound, never `Bottom` (the paper's instance rule).** From the POPL 2019 paper (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu, "Polymorphic Symmetric Multiple Dispatch with Variance", `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`; the authors could not prove the value's rule and replaced it, pp. 11:19, 11:25): such a parameter takes the intersection of its upper bounds, its declared bound (`Any` if none) under the constraint of the call's static return type; never `Bottom`, never the union of the arguments' types, never the value's type alone. "if I apply the rule that the ... later teams work supersedes the previous one, and you are saying the rule is coming from the paper and it helps us cleanly resolve something, then I will trust the team's work over whatever my misunderstanding of the things are." Which declaration runs stays the conversion rule above. MicroGPT's static types are concrete, so it is unaffected. Built in the specification: the dispatch paragraph and the inference chapter state the rule, with a callout that both implementations take the value's type where nothing fixes the parameter, walk by necessity (it has no static types) and the compiled path until phase 5 (FACTS, "The specification gives the run-time instance of a dispatched declaration by the POPL 2019 paper's rule ..."); the recheck's smaller sentences are in as defaults, listed for his review. Walk keeps row 157's fix as its best; the compiled path's departure is gated by one expected-failure pair where the two rules differ (row 538), beside the two for row 496's compiled crashes; the lone-parameter tests are plain tests of the bound (`InferLoneBound`, `InferLoneBoundWalk`), the unbounded case their expected failures (row 516). In batch 8: one checker rung binds an inference variable with no lower bound to its bounds instead of `BOTTOM`, with row 447's and row 425's tests and the union candidate made `Any`. Later: a walk rung for row 424, and phase 5's dispatcher carrying the call's static return type (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2048`). The three `extends Object` bounds written on `builtinPrimitive`, `fail` and `List`'s nullary comprehension to reach `Bottom` under the old solver go, the library back to the team's unbounded declarations, since under the instance rule they refuse every call where `()` is expected (item 20): "Yes, put the library back to the team's own declaration".
48	- **The order of the checker's attempts at a call** (row 508): the checker tries a call by subtyping without the expected type first and keeps that attempt when its result converts to the expected type, then tries coercion with the context, so a declaration that fits the arguments as they are is not passed over for one reached by coercion. One checker rung in batch 8; `XXXInferContextKeepsFit` promoted.
49	- **Walk chooses coercions on the value, for now.** Walk has no static types, so it chooses a coercion on the value where the specification's coercion chapter and the compiled path resolve it statically (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:619-662`; `XXXCoercionStaticRungC`, `XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC`); accepted as the interpreter's limit, stated in one S1 callout at that passage (`:663-675`); item 16 is closed with those two tests as its record. # Pavol's positions, decisions and known ground

## The goal

- **The measuring stick.** Finish what the designers intended, judged by the specification in `Specification/`, the Working Draft of 2010-12 as the revival revises it, with the 2012 Types chapter cited beside it; not redesign the language. The measure is one program, microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast. A pure-Java microGPT is written later as the floor to measure against. The specification is a living document that reflects the changes we make. The tree is tagged `sealed-tree` at the map's last commit; commits after it edit the original sources, test-driven.
- **How he weighs his calls where the designers left no word.** "I don't care about type theoretical purity and I'm accepting all unfinished corners of the language because I want to get to a compiled version of micro GPT. And I think this is the right pragmatic approach so that we do not get bogged down in weeds. Theory. We want to get this one program running fast. That's our guiding star. But along the way, I want to stay true to the spirit of Fortress." He has not read the specification, the papers on its type system or the library, and relies on the record: "I assume those people knew much more than I do right now." The check he asked for is a thorough top-tier review of every decision of his against the designers' intent, for errors of commission and of omission (`reviews/decisions-review/evidence.md`, `judgement.md`, `popl-recheck.md`); its items are decisions below.
- **The readable expression.** The toy problem is microGPT and the search is for its most readable expression: "we are searching for the optimal expression of the microGPT algorithm for readability." Fortress's mathematical notation and Iverson's APL notation (with Hsu's data design for data-flow algorithms) are the two sources. The Hsu-style flat program gave "a few lumps of coal", not a diamond; the vocabulary is where any polishing happens. C4 is the APL target form; C2's tuple hyperparameter form is what a strand assignment expands to; the semicolon form is set aside.
- **The APL side quest is closed.** It was a curiosity, then a ladder to learn APL, then native code (not an interpreter in an interpreter) with microGPT as its target; its remaining ground (tacit, characters, nested arrays) is not pursued.
- **The 2D notation is a gimmick.** Fortify's mathematical rendering is "a neat gimmick, not a good idea": it encodes one perspective on a computation into the syntax, while the same mathematics can be written many ways; APL's glyph-per-transformation is the purer realisation. Presentation only, not on the path, not an argument for Fortress; no work on it unless he asks.
- **The type checker on interpreter programs.** He wants the checker, which runs only on the compile path, usable on interpreter programs, and considers it low-hanging fruit. It comes after the switch-over, when walk also takes the static coercions the checker inserts (the entry on walk's choice of coercions).

- **The project's end.** DARPA's HPCS did not take Sun into phase three (2006) and the project lived on at Sun Labs until 2012. His reading: they did no work on performance, "mucked around with syntax", and the promise that a sufficiently advanced compiler would later make mathematical types fast was never true; the funding was pulled for good reason.

### How we work

- **Test first, the test kept.** Every sealed-tree edit starts from a failing test added to the corpus: the worker writes the test first, verifies that it actually fails, makes the fix, proves it passes, and the test stays in the corpus from then on; the full suite stays green. The unacceptable process is the one-off validation script, proving once by hand that the interpreter and the compiler agree and leaving no permanent check. The batches fix the issues the explorations captured as ledger rows, each with how to reproduce it, "Those are like our bug reports": the worker first commits the reproduction into the test suite, "this is how I have reproduced what the previous probe has discovered", then makes the fix, and the test passing demonstrates that the issue is fixed; "There isn't much more to it." The test captures the essence of the problem, not the shape the probe met it in, "do not blindly transpose the issue from the probe like think about it what's the core problem and capture that", written as a clean minimal version. Whether the test was seen failing first is read from the worker's transcript, not shown by a committed capture. The skeptic checks it there and runs no build to repeat it: "It should just check that the procedure of test first was followed. Not that it should be repeating the whole process, that is a fucking waste." Whether the suite runs per edit or per landed batch is an engineering choice, and per batch is in line with the rule. Every measured and repaired defect gets a gated assertion, a deferred spec-settled one an `XXX` test.
- **The suite's verdict is the check.** A test passes or fails, as the team designed the suite, and a value that matters is asserted in the test with the mechanisms the suite already has (an `assert` in an interpreter test, `run_out_equals` in a compiled one): "what is the purpose of a test suit that you just cannot run it and get a green? If everything that's encoded in it is, is okay and it turns red if it's not, why would you have to compare some values that it outputs? Those values must be part of the test." What a test prints beyond its checks does not matter: "When the designers of the test suite decided that it passes without any additional check, it is not needed to control its outputs." So no batch compares the corpus's printed outputs, no baseline is run to compare against, and no expected-output files are added to the interpreter suite, which has none; none of it is offered to him again.
- **Nothing is built or run twice on the same code.** "We don't want to re be rebuilding stuff that doesn't need to be rebuilt." The design, agreed with him and built into the batch script: the old code, the batch's base, is built once per batch, by the coordinator, before the launch, in a worktree nobody compiles or runs in (the script's `args.baseBuild`); "We just mechanically take the latest build and share it between each rung from the same baseline": every rung worktree is seeded from that one build in seconds (`coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh`), never built clean (his "Duh!" to "seeding a worktree by copying a built tree rather than rebuilding it"); the worker builds only what its own edit changed; the skeptic builds nothing, "very smart skeptics that just like reuse everything that was built during the rank phase as much as possible and just do their independent checks": it reads test-first from the worker's transcript, runs its own small programs on the new code with the rung's build and on the old code against the batch's one base build, through the rung's private seeded copy of it so that no two agents compile into one cache; the second skeptic checks only the repair against its own refusal; no stage re-runs a build, a suite or a measurement on a code state another stage has already run, and no agent reads again a log of output that has not changed: "I want to eliminate all waste of this type. Where we are re-executing stuff for no reason." How a worktree is seeded and what a worker clears after an edit or a failed build is engineering, measured before it is built into the batch script (`coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md`; the blinded engineers' variants in `coordinator/process-engineering/cache-sharing.md`).
- **The coordinator watches what it launches.** Only a long or large run the coordinator launches outside a batch, a probe that builds and runs suites for an hour or more, is watched against the estimate it was launched with, so that none runs away as probe P1 did (`coordinator/process-engineering/p1-cost.md`); when it passes its estimate the coordinator reacts, by an instruction to the worker or a stop, and its brief carries what keeps it efficient, a wait polled under the prompt cache's life among it. Ordinary workers carry no such procedure, and no ask is added before a probe: "I don't want you to become paranoid about running probes"; "I don't want the cargo cult of ... monitoring here. Only longer runs. ... I don't want you to burden with ... procedure on each call to workers." P1's waste was one the worker knew how to avoid: "an instruction to that worker would have corrected it."
- **A deeper pass, not a halt.** When something goes wrong or turns out undecided, the answer is a deeper pass, not a halt or a rollback. On a red gate over a merged batch, no bisection of commits: "we should identify the source of the conflict holistically and rework that part in the merged batch", because the goal is one tree with everything running rather than the largest subset that happens to be green. On a divergence the specification does not settle, no stop: "it is not a reason to stop the climb, it is the reason to think harder, review the architecture and holistically decide on the best path forward and execute that one." What reaches him are the forks already reserved in `PLAN.md`, not new ones invented at the point of difficulty.
- **Forks are probed before a batch is briefed.** "if there are known decision forks, which we can evaluate using probes, we should be doing these during this phase, during this planning phase": a fork a probe can settle is probed first, so that the decision is his and the worker gets a clean task, never a decision left to a worker and reviewed after the fact. Rows are taken one per message with refreshers (other languages, what makes sense in a high-performance language), not in groups.
- **A brief describes the problem, not the solution.** "How do we prevent the myopic view? … I want to have full creativity of solutions": a worker that has not read our notes lists every way the language and the library offer before a design choice reaches him; a rule that blocks an option is answered with how the library gets around it (protocol principle 2). A worker that records timings records the CPU too, so that comparisons can be guessed at.
- **The mission briefing.** "this whole exercise is about in-context learning. You were not pre-trained on Fortress. And the language was not finished." The planner, who has the whole map, gives each rung a mission briefing from the map that its agents read in their first turn; the share of agents that use it is reported with each landing (it was about 80% once and fell to 25-35%: "We need to get back to that level"). The briefing is in neutral words, "the decisions on record" ("I am trying to stay humble and I don't want to see my name in there multiple times. Make this neutral."); the worker answers no required questions about its search ("I disagree with the procedural enforcement here ... it's giving the agent side quests that it's graded on instead of something that it should just take into consideration during the implementation"; the briefing says "this is not a Java, this is not a Scala, you are in unfamiliar territory", and then the worker "should focus on its tasks"); the skeptic checks the result against the library's way, the ledger and sibling sites, and the decisions on record.
- **No re-measuring what the record holds.** "you are wasting resources on remeasuring." A brief hands over what the record has measured as findings to cite and names the one new thing to measure; a clean worker is clean of our options, not of our measurements (protocol principle 5). A rung whose test is the checker-count or distance stage takes the last landed gate's tables as its before and does not re-run the stage on an unchanged base; the gate commits its per-site list so that the before is complete. The nine steps are a way to brief him on unfamiliar ground, a type-theoretical question answered from the theory, the rule and a few declarations; and one global rule is sought from type theory and the peers' implementations rather than a rule slapped on a rule ("I cannot be trusted to derive a rule that wouldn't break the whole system and be a hodgepodge of edge cases").
- **Reversible stops do not hold a batch.** A stop a batch record reserves for him (a model or APL line beyond the approved ones, an interpreter output a rung cannot account for): "These don't need me now. They are reversible things I can review later. Don't block start of next batches on these." It lands, the push and the next batch go ahead, and it is listed for his review (the protocol's first hard rule). An output difference the untouched tree already shows from run to run, the test's verdict unchanged, is not a stop but a ledger row ("we had a rule too stringent because the spirit of the test is still held"); a rung's small items go to the ledger for review, not to him one per message.
- **A blocking second review does not hold a green batch.** "we have enough rigor or robustness and backup in our processes after that, so that small failure in a rule should not be blocking ... landing large ships like this." After its one repair round, a merged-diff review that still blocks does not hold a batch whose gate is green: the batch lands, the review's remaining findings go to the next batch and are listed for his review, and the post-batch review follows. A red gate after its repair still stops a batch. Built into `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` and its manual. The merged-diff review itself stays inside the batch, once, beside the gate, as the check of the merged tree's records, the stops and the routing before the push; removing it and moving its checks to the review after the batch is not taken (Fable's review of the batch practice against the Opus review's; he sided with Fable).
- **A tests-only repair does not rerun the gate.** "we are being overly pedantic for no good reason with like how the gates are set up ... we have to be weighing costs and benefits and we are not skipping the test, we are adding the test, we are moving stuff to following batches, we are running reviews after the fact, so we will catch stuff that the rerunning of a gate is not." A repair after the gate that changes no source, library, checker, interpreter or specification file runs its new tests in the harness on the merged tree; the first gate's tables stand; the landing records the new tests beside them; a repair that changes code reruns the gate. The same weighing of cost against what a rule protects applies to every rule of the batch workflow. Built.
- **What a batch commits.** "the commit discipline in a branch should not be different from what you will be committing to the main. Like don't keep temporary shit around. We are backing up the transcripts anyway from all the workers. So if we need to dig up something, how the worker arrived at some point, we have the full transcripts." A worker commits, on its own branch as on `main`, only what `main` is to hold: the Fortress change, its tests, its report, the lines for the ledger, FACTS and the plan, and a script or tool that is reusable ("If that script that batch contributes a script that is reusable, it goes in there", such as the documented way of running the checker as a shadow); no captured outputs, logs, raw outputs, script copies or other scratch are committed anywhere; new issues go to the ledger, reports into the batch's report; the process, and whether a worker wrote its test first and saw it fail, is read from the workers' transcripts, which the backup keeps. Deleting the `wip/` branches after a gate is his own chore in the GitHub web page, and he is not reminded of it. Built into the script, its manual and the protocol.
- **Workers commit their own files as they go.** "Workers should be committing themselves as they go, focused their files only. Protects against container failures and stops from harness bothering you about uncommitted files." They push to their own `wip/` branches as they work; the wip branches are cleaned up after the gate; the workflow script lives in the repository, not only in a session; the coordinator pushes `main` every few minutes ("I hope we are committing as we go because I worry that the container will get reset"). A protocol hard rule.
- **Which tier runs what.** "You can spend as much Opus workers as you want." The highest-risk decisions touch all three of specification, interpreter and compiler, which may disagree, and the design intent has to be inferred from the breadcrumbs left in all of them; the cheaper tier gathers the evidence into a condensed brief, and the high-level judgement of what makes sense given all the signals and what design balance lets the project grow belongs to the top tier, because that is the work it is for. Workers are pinned to Opus by the alias, "to make that workflow future proof"; the expensive model is escalated only at decision points, "sparsely so that it doesn't have to gather all the context by running multiple tool calls". Sonnet is the tier for archaeology. Two workers launched on the wrong tier once cost him 1.7 million tokens "down the drain". The coordinating session runs on Opus, so that Fable's own weekly pool is kept "for more important work"; it moves to Fable at his word when the pool on all models is spent, and how the Opus trial is judged is in `coordinator/postmortem-2026-09-27-record-keeping.md`.
- **The judge's rulings.** A judge's first ruling on a rung or on the merged tree runs on Opus; a second ruling on the same rung or tree runs on Fable ("Second ruling is for Fable."), named in `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` (`judgeTier`), so Fable is spent only when a second ruling happens. The review's judge rules while the gate runs on, and the gate writes its outputs under `tmp/` until the commit stage. A second repair round is not taken; option (b), approvals with required corrections when the fix is already written, has not been put to him (parked, `PLAN.md`).
- **The Fable rule.** "whenever it touches those three aspects of uh, library specification and implementation we are running the fable so if you use it sparingly I can pre-approve every such decision." The coordinator runs a Fable judgement without asking, sparingly, for a design question that touches two or more of the specification, the library and the implementation, once an Opus worker's evidence or list of ways is on file and the record has been searched and does not already settle it; he learns of it when the judgement is put to him in the ask form. He is asked first for any other Fable worker: a question about the coordinator's own conduct or a new kind of process choice, one whose recommendation would reverse a decision of his, or one where he wants Fable and Opus working independently. The standing pre-approvals: a judge's second ruling, and the top-tier reviews of the batch records.
- **One review after every batch.** "run the conformance review after every batch", combined with the process review into one pass, since "the amortized cost here is well worth the benefit": one Opus reviewer, reading only, does the conformance review, the process measures against `reviews/process-review-6b-7-7R.md` (misses by kind, those of items in the rung's own briefing, map use, briefing cost, re-measuring) and the routing check; the coordinator files what it finds in `PLAN.md` at the landing.
- **The phase-3 batches run on a standing go.** "I think you just carry on running the sequence of batches, I'll do the reset when I do it, If it stalls for a bit, I hope we'll recover without interruption. No need to complicate our runs with synchronization." And: "these are pre-approved. I want you to do autonomous overnight run." Each batch launches when the one before it has landed and its record is ready with no question open for him; a question a record raises goes to him first, except overnight, when it takes its recommended default and is listed for his review unless the default would reverse a decision of his, in which case that batch waits and the repair batch takes the slot; a run stalled by the limits is resumed with `resumeFromRunId`. A top-tier review in place of each coming batch record, in the form of `coordinator/climb-batch-7-review.md`, needs no further ask. The order is `PLAN.md`'s: batch 8 next. "Go" starts background work only; a batch run needs his explicit go, which for phase 3 this standing go is.
- **The new batch practice, and what he expects of it.** The practice after the post-mortem of the batch practice: the synthesis of its two reviews and both archaeologies, written into the script, its manual and the protocol, the script reviewed, a batch record rewritten to it and run on it, the landed batches' committed scratch cleaned in parallel, all built; of the post-mortem's four remaining questions, the output comparison is settled by his own position ("The suite's verdict is the check."), the merged-diff review stays by his word ("A blocking second review does not hold a green batch."), new tests are named by topic, as he asked of the files named after batches, and the cleaning ran by kind on his rule that only the reports and the changes to the repository stay; the rest of the review loops inside a batch (no second review, a judge and a repair only for a finding in code) are the synthesis's defaults, in force. "You can now redeem yourself by fixing this and, and, and showing me that you can be token efficient and not do bullshit jobs that you invented yourself." Every step spends the fewest workers the step needs and measures nothing the record already holds.
- **The gate's comparisons.** A comparison masks Java line numbers, identity hashes and moved library positions, with every masked difference listed for him; the `testSystem` comparison is the sum of the four shards; a name comparison, red when a test that passed before is missing or failing, is a script change put to him on its own (parked, `PLAN.md`); row 366 waits; no route C entry goes into Proposed Features. A team test line the flat tower breaks is respelled keeping the value the test checks, no assertion deleted, every such line listed for him with its before and after.
- **Estimates in the project's units.** Estimates in days or weeks are not accepted; sizes are given in the units the project has measured (a rung, a worker session, a check run). "I'm on a max plan. Talk to me in tokens." Costs are given in tokens, never in dollars, and a token count counts writes only, cache writes and new input: "Token counts, always report only writes. Cached reads are de-facto free vis-a-vis writes."
- **Check-ins and stops.** A series of check-ins is spaced 45 minutes apart, since hourly ones risk "that this session KV cache is evicted and then the wake-up call pays the full" price; the one after a predicted process stop is a single extra. He sends messages at any time (a message during a turn is queued and kills nothing); he does not press stop while the session is working, including the seconds after a reply while the transcript backup runs; an accidental stop is said so, and the run is resumed, keeping every agent that had finished.
- **Where the work lives.** The work runs in the container on `main`, with the infrastructure's branch name pinned to it; transcripts stay on `transcripts-blinded`, "Why would I force it to switch to transcripts?", and the lineages are joined at analysis time; the container recovery procedure is a lesson about the remote container (`coordinator/remote-container.md`), not a ledger row. Everything of ours is under `explorations/` ("to remove confusion for any workers"); the inventory note's own move list waits on his reading (parked, `PLAN.md`). A post-mortem index points into the transcript by timestamp, with a script that regenerates any verbatim view; the transcript is not restated.
- **The record is public and names models on purpose.** The protocol's rule against model identifiers is the harness's rule for what Claude itself writes and pushes, not a mandate to strip provenance from records that name models on purpose; "We are doing this work in public … there is no need to censor anything"; nothing in a transcript or an index is held back from the tree for that reason. The classifier refused writing this reading into the protocol itself, so it lives here.
- **The record's form: an optimized build and a debug build.** FACTS and POSITIONS are the optimized build, "what is true about the repository snapshot at this moment in time", written timelessly: no dates, no provenance, no account of what changed when or what corrected what; the history files are the debug build, with the full provenance, his quotes at their dates and every earlier text. "I don't want you to be searching with a flashlight in a dark room. I want to give you a map of the territory." A worker or a coordinator appending to FACTS or POSITIONS needs no timestamps; where one is written, or an entry corrects an earlier one, the next consolidation moves that provenance into the history and rewrites the fact or the position without it, at full informational fidelity. FACTS is consolidated before each batch launches, since workers read it and pay the cost. A FACTS entry is the fact, its source and its test in a few lines, pointing to the report or record that holds the detail, and the rung entries already in the file are shortened so, each earlier text verbatim in the history, before batch 8 launches: his choice of option 2 when the growth history showed the batches' rung entries, about 14 KB a landed batch, as most of FACTS' growth. The files read at every boot hold a clean current state and do not need edits as the work moves; the narrative of how a landed rung established a fact is history.
- **The statement for the public record on the usage limit.** "let the public record state that I'm now doing unpaid testing job of Anthropic's cloud infrastructure in my open source repository that is normally doing open source research of agentic coding capabilities." The account's weekly limit on all models stopped a running batch after its rung workers; later turns and subagents were served while the limit still read reached; he did not activate the promotional credit the panel offered, and his reading since is that visiting its page activated it unknowingly and that the work served was the $250 promotional credit for the cloud product, support having told him the offer had expired, "which was not true" (`coordinator/usage-metering-2026-09-30.md`, "After the report"); the container was booted afresh at each wake once nothing kept the session busy; at his word the batch was resumed to see whether it survives such interruptions and finishes.

## How he wants to be spoken to

- **The register.** "Drop the smart Alec essayist register before I blow a fuse": plain sentences, no framing flourishes, no closing lines that sum up in a phrase; advice as instructions, not as observations; replies very brief, plain English, no internal jargon. A wall of text is one he cannot absorb; the failure mode "is focused on over-compressing into a clever turn of phrase, but utterly fails in communicating clearly." Label which part answers which question when several are asked; do not restate what is in this file or in FACTS.md; when a concept is new to him, define it (he asked for reshape, ravel, planes, gather, outer product, Ring, Field, nat parameters, matrix multiplication).
- **Asks and decisions.** Decisions are presented one at a time as: what we do, what it changes, with a default he can accept without reading the argument; the argument lives in the committed review, not in chat. An ask for a yes states, in the message itself, what the worker would do, what it produces, what it touches in the tree, what it costs, what the yes commits him to afterwards and what a no costs ("What are the consequences of the yeses? What does that work even want to do? ... this is just pressuring me to give approval without understanding"); one ask per message; no label stands in for an explanation, and a new name is defined in the sentence that uses it; the recommendation comes after the explanation, in one line, never instead of it.
- **Ownership.** "I need to maintain some ownership of this work, even if we are doing agentic coding … I did not know what you did. I need to know what you did. And I need to be aware of those choices and decisions because I am the one carrying the responsibility for the consequences as a director of this revival": every re-approval row is gone through in detail, grouped by theme, and the count of reversals is not the measure. A decision made inside a worker's report and recorded in one line is a decision not made; flag it to him at the time.
- **The coordinator's standing goal** is to model what Pavol already knows and where his context has gaps, and to fill those gaps with the minimal set of relevant facts at the level he needs to decide; machine tokens are spent on thinking so that human context is protected. This came out of a compaction that left him "out of control, unaware of crucial details" while the coordinator was "taking unauthorized initiative which compounded my sense of helplessness to steer the Fortress revival efforts". The coordinator's two hats: "executive assistant here in this Fortress Revival project, helping me, the director, find a way forward, and the analyst that finds out what the fuck happened, why, and how do we move forward".
- **While a batch runs**, no progress reports on it until it lands. He is on Central European time; check-in times are given to him in UTC and in his local time. The harness's stop-hook reminders about uncommitted or unpushed work are processed silently, declined without a word while work is in flight, and never mentioned to him. He reads on an iOS client that sometimes shows stale state; "is anything in flight" is answered from the tree, not from the UI.
- **Format.** "table formatted in this way is hard to read on mobile … we just need a list": no tables in chat, lists. "write the numbers just as K or M. I'm fine as a programmer understanding what a kilo is": never spelled-out thousands and millions, and a numbers message carries few numbers, each with its meaning. Time is spoken from the clock or the record (when a batch will probably land, when a check-in fires), never from feel, "yesterday", "this morning", "last night", when the events were minutes or hours apart (protocol § 3).

- `explorations/reviews/mie-probes/literature.md`: What the field did with the exclusion trade after 2012, searched 2026-09-23 with every claim cited to a URL or DOI: POPL 2019 (Park, Hong, Steele, Ryu) kept the invariant exclusion as an ancestor rule and checks the call's static return type at dispatch, which picks the instance of the declaration the arguments select and never another declaration (Lemmas 5.8 and 5.9), as Naden's second write-up, `Papers/RuntimeInstantiation/RTRinstantionTheory.tex`, proposed, not the option his `justificationOfRTR.tex` rejected (the full text in `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`); the in-tree Welterweight draft of 2012 is its precursor; two Oracle patents filed the day of Naden's write-up list a "Self-types meet … must form a forest" restriction that admits the tower's chain inside the rule, never published; Julia avoids the trade by single inheritance and gives up static soundness; X10, Java, Kotlin and Scala forbid double instantiation, C#, F#, Rust and Haskell allow it and resolve statically, Ceylon relaxes only variant parameters and has no overloading; Cecil, C#, Swift and Scala flatten the self-typed algebra; no published resolution of the tower conflict and no necessity proof were found; the sites that blocked the search are listed in its header.
- `explorations/reviews/mie-probes/patents-forest-rule.md`: The "Self-types meet" restriction of the 2012 Oracle patents (US 8,843,887 and 8,898,632), read from USPTO's scans: a generic that comprises exactly its parameter may be instantiated several times by one type if the instantiations are ordered by subtyping ("must form a forest"). A shadow `checkP` implementing it takes the interpreter's library from 103 errors to 37, lifting 48 of the 61 exclusion errors (tower, comparisons, `Maybe`) and keeping the 13 on the `DistributesOver` markers, but only with the library's F-bound read as self-typed. The probes (`mie-probes/forest/`) show that the forest alone does not keep a specialisation at an inner level sound: generic code at the level below gets the specialisation's result (`IncompatibleClassChangeError`). It needs a return type rule over every level below, `comprises T` read covariantly, and dispatch ordered to match; so it is a third route that keeps the rule, the tower and specialisation, at more checker work than dropping the rule.

- `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`: What is established about the language, the library and the runtime, each with its source and grouped by area; read whole at every session start and cited rather than restated; an entry that changes is rewritten in place, and superseded narrative moves verbatim to `FACTS-history.md`.
- `explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md`: What Pavol has decided, stated or already knows, with dates, in his words or a close paraphrase, so that none of it is re-asked or re-explained; read whole at every session start. Consolidated 2026-09-27 to the decisions in force: a built decision keeps its date, his deciding words and what it means now, a decision not yet built keeps the detail the coming work needs, and a replaced one leaves the file; the full text of a shortened or moved entry is in `POSITIONS-history.md` under the same date. Standing directives about how we work stay in `explorations/protocol.md`.
- `explorations/coordinator/map/README.md`: The territory map, assembled 2026-09-16 from the survey reports beside it. The terms, the thirteen facts of the system's shape and touch-this-affects-that describe the tree as it stands; the list of surveys, the answers to Pavol's questions of that day and the development loop are kept; the decisions and the path in order point to `coordinator/PLAN.md`.
- `explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md`: Part one: the 22 packages with sizes and the import graph, dead modules, both pipelines phase by phase, the cache, the runtime, native interop, the one-table divergence of the paths.
- `explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md`: Part two: the 53 chapters of the July 2012 draft and about 110 features with parser rule, checker class, interpreter, codegen and prelude locations; the mechanism layer, the tower with line numbers, what the compiler prelude has of it.
- `explorations/coordinator/map/test-coverage.md`: Part three: every test corpus and JUnit class, what 1,377 and 382 are made of, the two corpora that never meet, blind spots by module, loop timings and the finer-grained targets.

1	<!-- Handover note written by the coordinating session on 2026-09-14 and rewritten the same day after Runs C2 and C3 were integrated, so that the state of the C series and the APL side quest survives context compaction. Read this before touching either. Facts cite their files. The first section, added 2026-09-18, is where the work stands overall; the C series and the APL quest below it are parked. -->
2	
3	# The C series and the APL side quest: state and what comes next
4	
5	## Where the work stands
6	
7	The goal is to finish what the designers intended, judged by the specification in `Specification/`, the Working Draft of 2010-12 as the revival revises it, with the 2012 Types chapter cited beside it, not to redesign the language, with one program as the measuring stick: microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast (the root `CLAUDE.md` § Project goal; `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-16).
8	
9	The live thread is the one library. The interpreter's library (`FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`) is to become the library the compiler checks, and the work is to bring the compiled checker to accept it (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-21). Between that library and bytecode stands the checker, not desugaring or code generation; it reports 59 errors on the library since climb batch 7b (`FortressLibrary` 132 to 106 and `RangeInternals` 18 to 12 by rung L, the one library's refused overload families repaired by its own exclusions and `openRange`'s typecase: `MIN` 4, `MAX` 4, `openRangeHelper` 3, three juxtaposition and two `seq` errors gone, rung C's two `cond` errors cleared by L's api line), 75 from climb batch 7C (`FortressLibrary` 2 to 132 by rung Y, each error counted twice: `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause now checks as written, so the api's hierarchy pass no longer stops it and its 66 overloading and return-type errors are counted for the first time, row 459 closed; `RangeInternals` 18 unchanged), 10 from climb batch 7R (`RangeInternals` 42 to 18 by rung J, the one library's scalar ranges over `ZZ32` alone; `FortressLibrary` 2 unchanged), 22 from climb batch 7 (`FortressLibrary` 38 to 2, rung H having cleared the 18 instantiation-exclusion errors and the api still stopping at its hierarchy pass on `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause, counted twice, item 21 of `coordinator/PLAN.md`; `NativeArray` 44 to 0 by rung A's `tabulate`; `RangeInternals` 42 unchanged), 62 from climb batch 6's rung F, which flattened the number tower (`FortressBuiltin` 18 to 0, `FortressLibrary` 110 to 38, `RangeInternals` 78 to 42, `NativeArray`'s 44 unchanged), through batch 6b, 125 from climb batch 4 through batch 5, 103 before it (rung N's declared rise: the 22 `fill` overloading errors in `NativeArray` that the crash it removed had hidden; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-4/RECORD.md`, "The merged-diff review"), and the table of climb batch 7b's landing, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/gate/checker-count.txt`, is the next batch's comparand, as its distance table, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/gate/distance.txt`, with its per-site list at `compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`, is the next distance stage's: 598 distinct errors over the whole library under the setting `any`, 26 fewer than batch 6.5b's 624 (the overloading kind 148 to 123, rung L's families), which was three body errors in `FortressBuiltin`'s component fewer than batch N's 627, against batch 6.5's and 7C's 626, batch 7R's 627, batch 7's 940 and the baseline's 1,747 (`compile-ladder/gate-baseline/distance.txt`), reported and never red. Since `a2b4809a5` (2026-09-23) the count is reported and never red on its own, because a fix can raise it; the gate stays red on a crash line no rung declared, a stale shadow or a table with no total (`coordinator/FACTS.md` § The checker and the one library; `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, the checker count). The route on the checker's multiple instantiation exclusion, the rule that no type may be two different instantiations of one generic, which 61 of batch 5's 125 errors came from, is decided, and climb batch 6's rung F carried it out on the one library (`coordinator/FACTS.md`, "The one library's number tower is flat"): route A, the rule kept and the library's numeric tower flattened, with the interpreter taught coercion first (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-24; the brief `reviews/exclusion-design-brief.md`; route C measured whole in `reviews/mie-probes/route-c-experiment.md`). How a `nat` size is carried at run time is decided too: design B, a size given the same descriptor object a type argument has, filling the slot the code generator already reserves (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-24; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md`, revised after the three size probes and the cost measurement, `perf-probes/nat/size-probes.md`, `size-cost.md`). The two probes that precede the run-time size rung's brief landed on 2026-09-25 (`perf-probes/nat/size-rung-probes.md`): a number's descriptor made by the loader on first request or by a factory with no holder class gives the same answers, the worker's reading, not a decision, being the factory, and the choice is one of Pavol's answers before batch 5 (`coordinator/PLAN.md`); and B's dispatcher already tests `DOT`'s shared size for equality, so no fix is needed.
10	
11	Decided, in `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`: the goal and its measuring stick (2026-09-16); test first, the test written and seen failing before the fix and kept in the corpus from then on (2026-09-17); the workflow, with workers pushing to their own `wip/` branches, the script in the repository and the higher tier called only at a refusal, a stop or a red gate (2026-09-18), narrowed to a judge's second ruling on the same rung or tree (2026-09-24); unboxed `double[]` storage and the `nat` sizes taken together, as the team designed them (2026-09-19); the tier rule, workers on the cheaper tier and a worker on the top tier only with his permission (2026-09-20); one library, the interpreter's, with no new declaration in the compiler prelude and its three files deleted at the switch-over (2026-09-21); route A and design B (2026-09-24, above), and the rows batch 3.5 handed back, 379, 380/381 and 383 (2026-09-24); re-approval rows 39 and 40 (2026-09-24, 2026-09-25) and 47 (2026-09-26). On 2026-09-26: a judge's second ruling runs on Fable; workers commit their own files as they go (protocol § 5); rung C's stop answered "(a), push", so batch 4 landed as gathered and was pushed; rung O's fork, the specification's wrapping operators ∔, ∸ and ⨰ declared in the interpreter's library first, then the ten natives raising `IntegerOverflow`, which also decides row 348 for the specification's spelling; S1, the team's layered form for a change to the specification; the later Types chapter (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`) cited beside `Specification/` where it speaks; S2, rung S taking the judgement's per-example verdicts; the number chapters changing only in the flattening rung's batch; and the plan, `coordinator/PLAN.md`.
12	
13	What comes next is the plan Pavol approved on 2026-09-26, `coordinator/PLAN.md` (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-26, the plan): its six phases from batch 5 to microGPT running fast, his answers in the order they are needed, the four workers sent out that day (W1-W4) and the parked items are there and are not repeated here. What is in flight at a given moment is in the boot note (`coordinator/postmortem-2026-09-19/held-list.md`, under "Boot note to the resumed coordinator", which is kept current at every compaction).
14	
15	The last landing is climb batch 7b, the second run of `coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-7.md`, item 5 of the plan's phase 3 (`coordinator/PLAN.md`, "Phase 3. The checker at a true zero"): answer 9's overloading chapters, the Return Type Rule over every instance and the positional rule, walk's choice by declared domains and the one library's refused overload families. It was cut from `811053f15`, four rungs applied in the order C, S, W, L, the record's own, since no path is shared (S after C because it lands only with C and the gather checked S's text against C's landed tests; W after S so that its commit carries the correction of S's interpreter callout): C at `e2f1aa7e8`, S at `576b4c287`, W at `8f7e183d4` and L at `070ef39e5`, with the merged-diff review's corrections at `720db2671` (six `FACTS.md` entries given a first clause stating the present, row 461's note, review.1, review-routed.1 and review-routed.2 in `coordinator/PLAN.md`) and the landed hashes at `b0eb41516`: the gate green on `070ef39e5` at its first run (`testFast` 1,731 tests in 48 suites, the compiler track 959, batch 6.5b's 899 and the batch's 40 `.test` files, C's 34, S's gather's 4 and L's gather's 2, `LibraryJUTest` 86, every other suite at its last landed count; `testSystem` 470, batch 6.5b's 451 and 19 files, W's 17 added and one deleted and L's 3; the checker count 59 against 75, all from rung L's families (`MIN` 4 to 0, `MAX` 4 to 0, `openRangeHelper` 3 to 0, juxtaposition 4 to 1, `seq` 5 to 3), rung C's two `cond` errors cleared by L's api line, the crash row `none`, the shadow matching; the distance stage, reported and never red, 598 against 624, the overloading kind 148 to 123 and the component bodies' 387 to 386, the classes `L1` 39 to 20, `M1` 109 to 103, `G1` 8 to 6 and `I1` 10 to 11, and five crash rows the same declarations moved by L's edit; the ladder's 85 files and the eighteen microGPT components unmoved; 42 of 42 four-thread `atomic` runs; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/gate/summary.txt`, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/gate/checker-count.txt` and `compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/gate/distance.txt`, the next batch's comparands, with `compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`), pushed (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/RECORD.md`, "The landing"). Both microGPT check programs, run under walk by the commit stage in the background, pass 40 of 40, exit 0 (`MicroGptFlatCheck` in 738 s, `MicroGptAplCheck` in 753 s; `tmp/gate-batch-7b/microgpt-walk/`, not committed). The specification was rebuilt once on the landed tree, 655 pages with no undefined reference. The run met the account's weekly limit: the script's dead-agent path read the failed skeptics and judges as refusals and drops, marked C, S and L dropped and started the gather with W alone, and the gather failing on the limit too is all that kept W from landing alone; the resumed run landed all four (`reviews/batch-7b-review.md`, section 3 and finding 1, routed to the script line of `coordinator/PLAN.md`). The stops met are lifted as reversible (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, "Reversible stops do not hold a batch."): rung S's skeptic's normative text for rules neither path runs, removed by the gather's corrections 1 and 2; the gather's text mismatch gather.1, the Meet Rule's closed-trait case for declarations with static parameters, which the text states and the checker refuses (row 546); and rung L's family whose only repair is a checker change, `seq`'s remaining pairs (row 556); rungs C and W met none. The rungs', the gather's and the merged-diff review's items for Pavol are entries under "Climb batch 7b, listed for his review" in `coordinator/PLAN.md`, with the stops and the rungs' lists; the combined post-batch review (`reviews/batch-7b-review.md`, `046cf4296`) finds all four rungs in the spirit of his decisions and of the designers, W's coverage trusting `comprises` clauses walk never checks (row 551), and its findings are routed in `coordinator/PLAN.md`, each at the home it names; none needs his answer before a batch. The batch's four rung paragraphs follow batch 6.5b's two and its review's. Before it, climb batch 6.5b landed, the second run of the repair batch of the plan's phase 2b (`coordinator/PLAN.md`, "Phase 2b. The repair batch from the conformance reviews"; `coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-6.5.md`), cut from the tree batch N's first run landed, two rungs applied in the order V, E, V first because its lowest edited line in the one path both touch, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, is the lower, which is also the record's order: V at `e455ccd98` and E at `413f36ac0`, with the gather's follow-up at `19c750c4a` (the `FACTS.md` text rung E's fold replaced, kept in `coordinator/FACTS-history.md`), the merged-diff review's corrections at `92c076b90`, the judge's ruling on that review at `b0ebf7e16`, its repair at `b6ee84f70` (row 528's run test, `ProjectFortress/library_tests/XXXRR32EqualityRungV.test`, keyed `run_out_contains=REACHED`, batch N's form, in place of the `run_out_contains=PASS` that the harness fails outright), the second review's corrections at `3c1687791`, the judge's ruling on the red gate at `ee0f277da` and the gate's repair, records only, at `cdc2e2a0e`: the gate on `19c750c4a` red on that one key alone (`testFast` 1,671 tests in 48 suites with 1 failure, `fast-library/LibraryJUTest` 86, batch N's 84 and V's two command lines, the failure `XXXRR32EqualityRungV`; the compiler track 899, batch N's 883 (its gate's 877 and its repair's six) and E's 16 command lines; every other suite at its last landed count; `testSystem` 451, batch N's 441 and ten files, E's eight and V's two, with no failure; the checker count 75, the table identical to batch N's, the crash row `none`, the shadow matching; the distance stage, reported and never red, 624 against batch N's 627, three body errors fewer, all in `FortressBuiltin`'s component (9 to 6), the classes `I1` +4, `I3` -1, `BR` -2 and `OT` -4, and six crash rows the same declarations moved by the batch's library lines; the ladder's 85 files and the eighteen microGPT components unmoved; 42 of 42 four-thread `atomic` runs; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-6.5b/gate/summary.txt`, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-6.5b/gate/checker-count.txt` and `compile-ladder/climb-batch-6.5b/gate/distance.txt`, the next batch's comparands, with `distance-sites.tsv` beside them), pushed (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-6.5b/RECORD.md`, "The landing"). # The C series and the APL side quest: state and what comes next

## Where the work stands

The goal is to finish what the designers intended, judged by the specification in `Specification/`, the Working Draft of 2010-12 as the revival revises it, with the 2012 Types chapter cited beside it, not to redesign the language, with one program as the measuring stick: microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast (the root `CLAUDE.md` § Project goal; `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-16).

The live thread is the one library. The interpreter's library (`FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`) is to become the library the compiler checks, and the work is to bring the compiled checker to accept it (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-21). Between that library and bytecode stands the checker, not desugaring or code generation; it reports 59 errors on the library since climb batch 7b (`FortressLibrary` 132 to 106 and `RangeInternals` 18 to 12 by rung L, the one library's refused overload families repaired by its own exclusions and `openRange`'s typecase: `MIN` 4, `MAX` 4, `openRangeHelper` 3, three juxtaposition and two `seq` errors gone, rung C's two `cond` errors cleared by L's api line), 75 from climb batch 7C (`FortressLibrary` 2 to 132 by rung Y, each error counted twice: `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause now checks as written, so the api's hierarchy pass no longer stops it and its 66 overloading and return-type errors are counted for the first time, row 459 closed; `RangeInternals` 18 unchanged), 10 from climb batch 7R (`RangeInternals` 42 to 18 by rung J, the one library's scalar ranges over `ZZ32` alone; `FortressLibrary` 2 unchanged), 22 from climb batch 7 (`FortressLibrary` 38 to 2, rung H having cleared the 18 instantiation-exclusion errors and the api still stopping at its hierarchy pass on `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause, counted twice, item 21 of `coordinator/PLAN.md`; `NativeArray` 44 to 0 by rung A's `tabulate`; `RangeInternals` 42 unchanged), 62 from climb batch 6's rung F, which flattened the number tower (`FortressBuiltin` 18 to 0, `FortressLibrary` 110 to 38, `RangeInternals` 78 to 42, `NativeArray`'s 44 unchanged), through batch 6b, 125 from climb batch 4 through batch 5, 103 before it (rung N's declared rise: the 22 `fill` overloading errors in `NativeArray` that the crash it removed had hidden; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-4/RECORD.md`, "The merged-diff review"), and the table of climb batch 7b's landing, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/gate/checker-count.txt`, is the next batch's comparand, as its distance table, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-7b/gate/distance.txt`, with its per-site list at `compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`, is the next distance stage's: 598 distinct errors over the whole library under the setting `any`, 26 fewer than batch 6.5b's 624 (the overloading kind 148 to 123, rung L's families), which was three body errors in `FortressBuiltin`'s component fewer than batch N's 627, against batch 6.5's and 7C's 626, batch 7R's 627, batch 7's 940 and the baseline's 1,747 (`compile-ladder/gate-baseline/distance.txt`), reported and never red. The block `gen10.py` writes is spliced into `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` in place of batch 9's, with `LEDGER_FROM` set (610 on this base, the ledger's highest row being 609), checked by `check10.js` as the harness parses it, and committed. **The batch rules.** Rule 1: holds, the shared files by section, declaration and entry (section 4). Rule 2: holds (section 4). Rule 3, one rung touching Java or Scala: does not hold, W rebuilds walk and C the checker in their worktrees; at two agents at a time at most two builds run at once, and no skeptic builds. Rule 4: k is 4, two agents at a time; the scatter starts the longest expected first, C, N, G, W (`expectedMinutes` 260, 240, 220, 200, guesses that set the order only; under P1, W's goes to 250 and runs second).

**The gate, and what it should show.** The comparands are batch 9's `summary.txt`, `checker-count.txt` (1) and `distance.txt` (340) with `distance-sites.tsv`. Expected:
- `testSystem`: the comparand's sum (504) plus the files W, G and N add; a promotion moves nothing.
- The compiler track: 1,010 plus the files C adds; the library track 86 (`library_tests`, unchanged); the other fast tracks unchanged.
- The four-thread `atomic` runs: unchanged.
- The ladder: no rung declares a move; each worker's subset is empty; the gate's ladder stage judges.
- The checker count and the distance: reported, never red; C, G and N move them, W cannot; no rung declares a prediction. By reading the rungs reach 148 of the 340 (C 13, G 57, N 60 and the drop's 18), and C's crash repairs and the export repairs may unmask errors; the crash rows may move.
- After the review's or the gate's repair, the gate runs again only when the repair, or the review's corrections, changed a path the gate reads that is not a test file (`ProjectFortress/`, `Library/` or `build.xml`); a repair of tests, records or specification text leaves the first gate's tables standing, recorded beside the summary (POSITIONS, "A tests-only repair does not rerun the gate." and "Nothing is built or run twice on the same code.").

**Provenance.** Each `REPORT.md` opens with the five-line provenance block, its `historical:` line naming every 2012-tree file the rung edits; every commit whose diff touches a path outside `explorations/` carries the same line.

**Ledger.** New rows numbered from `LEDGER_FROM`, in manifest order W, C, G, N. Closed with "fixed <commit>": 544, 534, 588 (W); 563, 593, 604, 605, 574 (C); 590, 602 and 560's first part (N), as each repair lands; the crash rows C opens and closes. Notes: 425 (W); 561, 597 (C); 488 (G); 577 (N). Under P1's answer, 424 and 555 closed (W).

**After the landing.** The combined post-batch review, as after every batch, measuring this run against batch 9's review as its before. P1 and its judgement, if they did not run before the launch. The next batch's record drafted from this batch's landed table, with item 36's checker change, the items Pavol answers among 37 to 42 and 38's families, P1's half if it waited, and the residue.

**The push.** The commit stage pushes `main` only when no landed rung carries a stop that was met and not lifted; every stop this record reserves for Pavol is reversible and lifted by POSITIONS, "Reversible stops do not hold a batch."

An `Agent`-tool worker continues from its transcript on a `SendMessage`.
